title: Characterization and Classification of Selected Soil under Different Land Fallow Length in an Ultisol in A Humid Tropical Environment
abstractText: The study was conducted to characterized and classify selected soil under different fallow length in an ultisol in Ihiagwa, Owerri, Imo state. A target survey was used for the study. Three profile pits were dug on; continuous cropping, three year fallow and seven years fallow. Soil samples were collected from each of the profiles according to their horizonation. The samples were subjected to laboratory analyses using standard procedures. Data obtained were analyzed using analyses of variance and coefficient of variation. The result shows that, the moisture content was higher in the three years and seven years fallow sites (9.54% and 9.89%) respective and least in continuous cropping (8.92%). The Bulk density was higher in the continuous cropping (1.33g/cm3) compared to the three years and seven years fallow that have (1.26g/cm3 and 0.85g/cm3) respectively. The three sites were moderately acidic . The three years and seven years fallow sites recorded high mean value in organic carbon, organic matter, total exchangeable base, and effective cation exchange capacity, compare to continuous cropping site that recorded low value in the soils. There was a low variability in the soil pH, medium variability in the Total Exchangeable acidity and high variability in the Total exchangeable base. The total porosity correlated positively with organic matter and the organic matter also correlated negatively with the bulk density. Using USDA and World Reference Base classification, the continuous cropping and three years fallow soil was classified as Arenic Kandiudults and Arenic Acrisols respectively while the seven years fallow was classified as Typic Paleudults and Chromic Acrisols respectively.

title: Model-embedded Gaussian Process Regression for Parameter Estimation and Uncertainty Quantification in Dynamical Systems
abstractText: The identification of dynamical systems is a vital task in science and engineering. Traditional methods require numerous calls to the dynamical-system solver, rendering likelihood-based or least-squares inference frameworks impractical. For efficient parameter inference, two state-of-the-art techniques are the kernel method for modeling and the one-step framework for jointly inferring unknown parameters and hyperparameters. The kernel method is a quick and straightforward technique, but it cannot estimate solutions and their derivatives, which must strictly adhere to physical laws. We propose a model-embedded one-step Bayesian framework for joint inference of unknown parameters and hyperparameters by maximizing the marginal likelihood. This approach models the solution and its derivatives using Gaussian process regression (GPR), taking into account smoothness and continuity properties, and treats differential equations as constraints that can be naturally integrated into the Bayesian framework in the linear case. Additionally, we prove convergence of the model-embedded Gaussian process regression (ME-GPR) for theoretical development. Motivated by Taylor expansion, we introduce a piecewise first-order linearization strategy to handle nonlinear dynamical systems. Numerical experiments on simulated linear and nonlinear dynamical systems evaluate the method’s performance in parameter estimation and in predicting solutions and their derivatives.

title: Matroid products via submodular coupling
abstractText: The study of matroid products traces back to the 1970s, when Lovász and Mason studied the existence of various types of matroid products with different strengths. Among these, the tensor product is arguably the most important, which can be considered as an extension of the tensor product from linear algebra. However, Las Vergnas showed that the tensor product of two matroids does not always exist. Over the following four decades, matroid products remained surprisingly underexplored, regaining attention only in recent years due to applications in tropical geometry and the limit theory of matroids. In this paper, inspired by the concept of coupling in probability theory, we introduce the notion of coupling for matroids -- or, more generally, for submodular set functions. This operation can be viewed as a relaxation of the tensor product. Unlike the tensor product, however, we prove that a coupling always exists for any two submodular functions and can be chosen to be increasing if the original functions are increasing. As a corollary, we show that two matroids always admit a matroid coupling, leading to a novel operation on matroids. Our construction is algorithmic, providing an oracle for the coupling matroid through a polynomial number of oracle calls to the original matroids. We apply this construction to derive new necessary conditions for matroid representability and establish connection between tensor products and Ingleton's inequality. Additionally, we verify the existence of set functions that are universal with respect to a given property, meaning any set function over a finite domain with that property can be obtained as a quotient.

title: The morphology and chemistry of Vepris wadigo sp. nov. (Rutaceae), an Endangered tree of Kenyan coastal forest with the description of wadigin, a newly named alkaloid
abstractText: Here we describe Vepris wadigo based on new collections and observations of the informally published Diphasia sp. A of the Flora of Tropical East Africa. Vepris wadigo is known with certainty only from Kaya Kinondo and Kaya Timbwa forests in Kwale District of coastal Kenya where it is known as Mchikoma (Digo language). Vepris is a genus of nearly 100 species, many of medicinal importance. They are evergreen, shrubs and trees, mainly of forest, confined to Africa and Madagascar with 1 species extending to Arabia and another endemic to India. Vepris wadigo is compared with the only other known diphasoid Vepris species of East Africa, Vepris morogoroensis of Tanzania. However, Vepris wadigo most closely resembles Vepris stolzii of Tanzania which differs in the 4-locular fruit. The chemistry of Vepris wadigo is unique among the African species of Vepris which have been analysed, since acridones, quinolines and limonoids, which characterise the genus were not detected. The six compounds characterised included a benzamide newly described and named in this paper as wadigin (N-(2,6-dihydroxybenzoyl)-O-methyltyramine) and four lignans and neolignans not previously found or very unusual in Vepris. Lupeol, found in other African Vepris, was also recorded. Vepris wadigo is here provisionally assessed as Endangered, EN B1ab(i,ii,iii)+2ab(i,ii,iii). Satellite imagery has shown that the area of the habitat has slowly decreased in recent decades.

title: Strategic evaluation of total quality management in the weaving industry using integrated DEMATEL–ISM methodology
abstractText: Purpose This research aimed to systematically identify, analyze and prioritize the critical enablers during the implementation of total quality management (TQM) in the weaving industry, thereby formulating strategic recommendations to improve quality performance and operational effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach The key enablers were identified based on the ISO 9001:2015 standard and previous research on the subject. The Delphi method was used to conduct an expert survey, and 12 selected experts evaluated these enablers using a Likert scale. The Python programming language was then used to perform Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) calculations, followed by the Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) methodology to construct a hierarchical model. Sensitivity analysis was conducted to examine the structural robustness of the DEMATEL-ISM integrated model. Stability Status was tested by giving a qualitative ranking to describe how dramatically an individual enabler moves within the hierarchy when different threshold boundaries are used. The second Delphi round was executed to validate the results. Findings The results of this research indicated that improving performance across all enablers of TQM within the established hierarchical structure in the weaving industry relied on effectively managing key enablers. DEMATEL analysis identified six enablers as primary causes (cause factors) and six others as effects (effect factors), whose performance was highly dependent on the successful management of the causal factors. ISM analysis further revealed two driving enablers placed as the foundation for the successful implementation of TQM, along with three dependent enablers whose effectiveness was determined by these driving enablers. Originality/value This research was used to guide the weaving industry to develop a strategic evaluation method to ensure responsiveness to quality performance and operational effectiveness.

title: ASSESSMENT OF SELECTED MACHINE LEARNING SYSTEMS IN PREDICTING THE RESILIENT MODULUS OF COHESIVE SOILS
abstractText: Characterizing subgrade soils in terms of resilient modulus (MR) is crucial for pavement design. However, the process can be expensive and time-consuming, leading to the need for more efficient alternatives. This research investigates the effectiveness of using machine learning systems to predict the resilient modulus of cohesive subgrade soils. A dataset of 400 resilient modulus measurements obtained from in-situ cone penetration tests waere collected, along with an additional 200 prediction data points from past research. The combined dataset were then divided into training and testing subsets and used to develop two machine learning predicting systems: Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN). The performance of these systems was evaluated using the sum of residuals (R) and the Mean Square Error (MSE) performance index. Among the SVM models tested, the one trained with a medium Gaussian kernel demonstrated the best predictive capability. For the BPNN, the most effective configuration included four input variables, fifteen hidden neurons, and thirty-three epochs. The BPNN system outperformed the SVM system, yielding higher predictability with training and testing R values of 0.98 and 0.92, and MSE training and test values of 19.84 and 90.16, respectively. In contrast, the SVM system produced training and testing R values of 0.92 and 0.72, with MSE training and test values of 47.75 and 223.73. This research demonstrates that machine learning systems can accurately predict the resilient modulus of soils, providing acceptable error levels for pavement design and construction.

title: Exploring Scape Anatomy in Crocus L. (Iridaceae): a comparative study of 24 taxa from Türkiye
abstractText: This study aimed to evaluate the taxonomic significance of scape anatomy for species delimitation and infrageneric classification in 24 selected Crocus taxa from Türkiye. Furthermore, it assessed the consistency between anatomical patterns and molecular evidence (nrITS data) to explore the utility of scape characters in integrative systematic studies. Scapes from 25 specimens belonging to six series were analyzed. Cross-sections from three regions (distal, central, and basal) were examined using light microscopy, with the middle section identified as the most stable for analysis. Nineteen anatomical parameters were recorded and analyzed. Statistical methods were applied alongside Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of nrITS data. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) results separated the specimens into six distinct groups corresponding to the series. Notable differences were found between flowering seasons: autumn-blooming species typically exhibit larger, rounder scapes with square-shaped styloid crystals, whereas spring-blooming taxa have more vertices and small styloids. Scape anatomical patterns showed a general agreement with ITS-supported clades, suggesting that scape characters may reflect genomic differentiation rather than ecological. These findings demonstrate that the fruiting scape is a valuable tool for Crocus systematics and support its inclusion in integrative taxonomic frameworks.

title: Distinguishing between cost and value of psychological interventions: The case of long- versus short-term therapy
abstractText: Background Psychotherapy has been proven in numerous clinical studies to be an evidence-based intervention for many mental disorders. However, the question of the necessary “dose,” usually quantified as the number of therapy sessions, is a subject of ongoing debate. While proponents of long-term therapy emphasize significant but small additional effects, skeptics point to highly heterogeneous findings and escalating costs. Method Using realistic assumptions about costs, benefits, and resource constraints of psychotherapy, we calculated the long-run public health impact of longer versus shorter therapies. Specifically, we incorporated training costs, limited availability of trained therapists, and short- versus long-term recovery trajectories. Results Our simulation shows that, even under optimistic assumptions, short-term therapies achieve more remission-years per unit of cost than long-term therapies. A web application is provided to explore our calculations with customizable parameters and presets based on existing outcome studies. Conclusion The discussion of the potential benefits of longer therapies should be expanded to include not only clinical outcomes and therapy dose but also total treatment costs, including training requirements and therapist availability, in cost-effectiveness calculations.

title: Rapid polarization position angle variations in FRB 20240114A point to a magnetospheric origin
abstractText: Fast radio bursts (FRBs), thought to originate from magnetars, exhibit diverse polarization properties that provide key constraints on their emission physics and local magneto-ionic environments. Among these, the polarization position angle (PPA) is particularly sensitive to magnetic-field geometry in the emitting region and propagation effects in the magnetosphere and beyond. In hyperactive repeating FRBs, the PPAs are typically stable across the duration of a burst and, in two well-studied cases, remain stable on timescales of hours to days. In contrast, here we present observations of the repeating source ̊onefourseven that show significant burst-to-burst jumps in the PPA. Using full-Stokes, high–time-resolution observations from the Nançay Radio Telescope (1.1--1.8 GHz) and the Effelsberg 100-m telescope (1.3--1.5 GHz) spanning ∼1 year, we measure burst rotation measures (RMs), as well as time-resolved polarization fractions and PPAs at 12 epochs. The burst RMs remain stable across all epochs, and the emission is predominantly highly linearly polarized, with sim81% of bursts showing L/I > 0.8, while circular polarization is weaker (sim16% with $|V/I| > 0.1$). We find no evidence for Faraday conversion. The PPA exhibits rapid, stochastic variations on timescales from milliseconds to hours, spanning the full range of pm90 degrees during two periods of high activity and ±50 degrees in a third active period. We also investigate the statistics of PPA jumps, defined as the difference in PPA between two consecutive bursts. We find that: (1) there is no difference in the distribution of jumps on timescales shorter or longer than 1 s; (2) positive and negative jumps are equally likely; and 3) a jump of ±90 degrees, as expected from, for example, orthogonal mode jumps, is not more common than any other value. No other hyperactive repeaters show this combination of relatively stable RM, consistently high linear polarization, and extreme burst-to-burst PPA variability. The observations disfavor emission from a single fixed region in a rotating magnetosphere and instead point toward multiple emission regions, or strong magnetospheric propagation effects, and/or propagation effects in the foreground medium, such as plasma lensing.

title: Fractional CO₂ laser for eyelid and periorbital wrinkles and laxity: short- and long-term clinical results using a standardized protocol
abstractText: Objective Eyelid and periorbital rejuvenation is a common aesthetic concern. This study aimed to describe an original and detailed fractional CO₂ laser protocol and evaluate its efficacy and safety for skin tightening and wrinkle reduction in the upper and lower eyelids and periorbital region, with 12-month follow-up. Materials and Methods A single-arm, evaluator-blinded clinical trial was conducted in 27 patients presenting with eyelid and periorbital laxity and wrinkles. All patients underwent a single session of fractional CO₂ laser treatment. Clinical outcomes were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months using two study-specific grading scales evaluated by two independent expert assessors, along with patient-reported outcomes. Results Significant reductions were observed in eyelid and periorbital laxity (p < 0.0001) and in fine lines and wrinkle depth (p < 0.0001). At 3 months, 74% of patients achieved good overall improvement (50–75% correction; p < 0.0001). Improvements were maintained over time with minor variations, including a peak effect at 6 months followed by a slight decline at 12 months. At 12 months, 70% of patients reported being satisfied or very satisfied. No unexpected adverse events or complications were observed. Conclusion The protocol described appears to be a safe and potentially effective approach for eyelid and periorbital rejuvenation, associated with improvements in skin tightening and wrinkle reduction, with high patient satisfaction and results generally maintained over at least a 12-month follow-up.

title: The relationship among emotional intelligence, self-efficacy, and attitude toward death in family caregivers of patients with advanced cancer
abstractText: Background As the global incidence of cancer continues to rise, most patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage because early symptoms are often nonspecific or overlooked. In the care of patients with advanced cancer, family caregivers assume the primary caregiving responsibilities. At the same time, they must confront end-of-life and death-related events, which place considerable demands on their emotional and caregiving capacities. However, research examining how family caregivers’ emotional intelligence influences their attitudes toward death through self-efficacy remains very limited. Aims To explore the associations among emotional intelligence, self-efficacy, and attitudes toward death in family caregivers of patients with advanced cancer, and to analyze the mediating role of self-efficacy in these relationships. Methods This quantitative cross-sectional study used convenience sampling to recruit 365 family caregivers of patients with advanced cancer from three hospitals in Hunan Province, China. The Wong and Law Emotional Intelligence Scale (WLEIS), the General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES), and the Attitude Toward Death Profile-Revised (DAP-R) were used to assess participants. Results Among family caregivers of patients with advanced cancer, emotional intelligence was positively correlated with self-efficacy and with the neutral acceptance dimension of attitudes toward death, and negatively correlated with death fear. Self-efficacy was negatively correlated with death fear and positively correlated with neutral acceptance. Self-efficacy played a partial mediating role in the relationships between emotional intelligence and attitudes toward death. Conclusion This study found significant associations among emotional intelligence, self-efficacy, and attitudes toward death in family caregivers of patients with advanced cancer, with self-efficacy partially mediating these relationships.

title: A market-initialised accelerated failure time model for in-play football forecasting
abstractText: In-play football forecasting models are rarely compared with betting exchange prices, which aggregate information from many market participants. We make this comparison for several goal-arrival models, focusing on a Weibull accelerated failure time model with two extensions: initialising team strength parameters from Betfair Exchange prices at kick-off to capture pre-match market information, and including cumulative shots as a time-varying covariate to capture in-play information. The initialisation, which fits team-strength parameters to 1X2 and over/under prices by squared-error minimisation, applies to any intensity-based goal arrival model. Evaluated across 280 English Premier League matches at minute intervals, the market-initialised model remains measurably weaker than Betfair in-play prices (classification accuracy 68.5 % versus 69.5 %, ranked probability score 0.1325 versus 0.1281), but retains interpretable team-level parameters and covariate effects. A comparison with a market-implied Poisson model, a Cox process and a Bayesian birth process, all initialised from the same pre-match odds, confirms that market initialisation is the dominant driver of predictive accuracy. A betting simulation against Betfair in-play odds yields a 1.0 % return on investment over 37,467 bets (95 % interval −3.8 % to 5.9 %), which we regard as preliminary given the limited sample of matches and prices that may not have been executable.

title: A noise-resistant anonymous batch authentication scheme for the Internet of Vehicles based on quantum graph states
abstractText: 在信道高度开放与边缘节点弱信任的复杂背景下, 车联网(Internet of Vehicles, IoV) 大规模并发认证常面临串谋风险增长以及纠错开销冗余的现实困境. 为此, 本文提出一种基于物理与应用双层协同防御架构的批量认证方案. 该方案核心在于利用完全图态特有的稳定子关联特性, 将物理层校验与应用层掩码联合, 从机制上阻断了内部节点的合谋路径. 针对硬件限制, 方案引入即收即测机制以规避对量子存储器的刚性需求, 并采用经典多数投票策略缓解信道误码干扰. 安全性论证指出, 本方案在常规外部攻击下具备物理层统计安全属性；而在极端内部串谋场景中, 则凭借应用层动态掩码构建起计算安全防线, 确保在对抗各类量子及经典攻击时, 均能满足完全前后向保密与轨迹不可链接性. 实验数据表明, 该方案成功将终端计算开销缩减至0.941ms, 即便是处于恶劣信道环境下, 仍能达成99.9999% 的超可靠低延迟通信指标, 充分证实了其在车联网实际部署中的普适性.

title: Preoperative depression as a neuroimmune-cholinergic vulnerability state for postoperative cognitive dysfunction after gastrointestinal cancer surgery
abstractText: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction, a legacy term broadly corresponding to the postoperative spectrum within the contemporary perioperative neurocognitive disorders framework, is a frequent and clinically consequential complication after gastrointestinal (GI) cancer surgery in older adults. Preoperative depression is increasingly recognized as a high-impact risk factor, yet its biological links to perioperative brain vulnerability remain underappreciated. Li et al recently published a study in World Journal of Gastrointestinal Surgery , examining postoperative cognitive outcomes in depressed older adults undergoing GI tumor surgery, with particular emphasis on inflammatory and cholinergic mechanisms. Li et al report a substantial burden of postoperative cognitive impairment and identify a dual-pathway pattern in which postoperative inflammatory signaling - indexed by interleukin-6 as a representative perioperative cytokine - and reduced peripheral cholinesterase activity are associated with excess cognitive risk in patients with preoperative depression. Conceptually, these findings support reframing depression as a neuroimmune-cholinergic vulnerability state that may amplify perioperative susceptibility through interacting inflammatory and neuromodulatory processes. While mechanistic in nature and hypothesis-generating, this framework suggests that preoperative depression screening may inform future risk stratification strategies and motivate investigation of inflammation-aware, cholinergic-sensitive, and psychosocially integrated perioperative care approaches. A neuropsychiatric-immune-cholinergic perspective provides a coherent conceptual framework for understanding heterogeneity in postoperative neurocognitive outcomes after GI cancer surgery and highlights preoperative depression as a biologically relevant vulnerability state warranting further prospective investigation.

title: Probing a New Subclass of Low-Luminosity Gamma-Ray Burst–Supernovae: Insights from EP250304a and SN,2025fhm
abstractText: With the advent of the ( ) mission, we are entering a new era in the study of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), enabling the detection of faint, low-luminosity transients that would previously have gone undetected. EP250304a was an event discovered by associated with the broad-lined type Ic supernova (SN) SN,2025fhm located at Einstein Probe EP EP z = 0.2. Despite no gamma-ray emission being detected at the time of the trigger, we identified evidence of a relativistic outflow consistent with a GRB-like jet across multiple wavelengths. We present a detailed spectral and photometric analysis of EP250304a/SN,2025fhm, including multi-band light curve modelling performed with the EP Redback Python package. we found that this event closely resembles low-luminosity GRB-SNe (llGRB-SNe) such as GRB,060218/SN,2006aj, GRB,100316D/SN,2010bh, and GRB,171205A/SN,2017iuk, all of which exhibit early-time emission consistent with a thermal shocked cocoon. These similarities suggest that EP250304A/SN,2025fhm may belong to an emerging subclass of shocked cocoon-dominated llGRB-SNe, representing the low-luminosity end of a broader continuum of engine-driven GRB-SN explosions.

title: When bars and spirals conspire: Recurrent build-up of the nuclear regions of disc galaxies
abstractText: The assembly history of the central regions of disc galaxies is regulated by dynamical processes that trigger gas infall events and lead to active star formation in nuclear stellar discs and in nuclear stellar clusters. In the Milky Way, recent studies of its nuclear regions have revealed a complex star formation history, with an initial burst associated with the formation of the Galactic bar followed by a non-constant star formation rate. In this work, we study the formation and evolution of nuclear structures as well as the link between the formation of large-scale structures and the nuclear stellar disc and star cluster. Our goal is to investigate the effects of the bar and spiral arms on the dynamics of the gas and, as a result, on the star formation history of nuclear stellar structures. To this aim, we ran and analysed a simulation of an isolated Milky Way-like galaxy with the SWIFT N -body plus hydrodynamics simulation code, including star formation and stellar feedback from supernovae types Ia and II. We start from a live dark matter halo and a pre-existing stellar and gaseous disc with a 20% gas fraction, which quickly forms a bar, a boxy-peanut bulge, spiral arms, and nuclear structures. We studied the star formation history of these regions and how they relate to variations in the galactic bar length, strength, and pattern speed. We also investigated the role of spiral arms and their interaction with the bar. We find that the star formation history of the nuclear regions displays a main burst at the time of the formation of the bar due to bar-driven gas inflows. After bar formation, we found secondary regularly spaced star formation bursts that do not appear in the disc star formation history. These secondary bursts occur when the spiral arms and the bar -- which rotate at different pattern speeds -- reconnect, triggering secondary gas inflow events. The interaction of spiral arms and the galactic bar can enhance non-axisymmetric features in the disc, and thus trigger bar-driven gas infall even after the bar has formed. Our simulation suggests that these bar-spiral reconnection events are imprinted in the star formation history of the nuclear stellar clusters and nuclear stellar discs as episodic star formation bursts.

title: Value of pancreatic duct stent placement combined with octreotide for reducing the postoperative pancreatic fistula rate in patients with diabetes undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy
abstractText: BACKGROUND Pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) carries high postoperative complication risks, and postoperative pancreatic fistula is most common. Diabetes further elevates this risk due to impaired healing and immunity. Pancreatic duct stents and octreotide are widely used for prevention, but relevant studies targeting diabetic patients remain insufficient. This study explored the combined application of the two interventions. AIM To investigate the effect of combined therapy on postoperative pancreatic fistula in diabetic PD patients. METHODS Data from 156 patients with diabetes who underwent PD at our hospital from January 2022 to September 2025 were collected. The patients were divided into a combination group and a control group. In the control group, pancreatic duct stent was placed intraoperatively and routine postoperative care was given. In the combination group, intravenous octreotide infusion was added postoperatively. The incidence of postoperative pancreatic fistula, duration of drain retention, glycemic variability, and length of hospital stay were compared between the two groups. RESULTS A total of 60 patients were included in each group, and baseline characteristics were comparable. The incidence of postoperative pancreatic fistula in the combination group was 11.7%, significantly lower than that in the control group (23.3%; odds ratio = 0.43, 95%CI: 0.21-0.89, P = 0.022). The combination group also had significantly shorter drain retention days (8.8 ± 3.5 days vs 12.1 ± 4.8 days, P = 0.018) and postoperative hospital stay (14.5 ± 5.3 days vs 19.2 ± 7.1 days, P = 0.026). No significant inter-group differences were found in mean blood glucose, blood glucose coefficient of variation, daily insulin dosage and the incidence of hypoglycemic events (all P > 0.05). CONCLUSION In diabetic patients undergoing PD, the combined regimen was associated with a reduced incidence of postoperative pancreatic fistula, shorter drainage duration, and a shorter hospital stay without significantly affecting postoperative glycemic variability.

title: Dissecting the obscured core of GN20: An active galactic nucleus outshone by star formation
abstractText: We investigated the relative contributions of star formation and active galactic nucleus (AGN) activity to the total energy budget of GN20, one of the most luminous dusty star-forming galaxies known at z>4, through spatially resolved spectral energy distribution (SED) decomposition. We performed Bayesian SED fitting with CIGALE on two spatially distinct apertures --- the nuclear core (r=0.14 ∼1 kpc physical) and the full galaxy (r=1.4 9.9 kpc) --- combining JWST/NIRCam and MIRI broadband imaging, JWST/NIRSpec PRISM integral field unit pseudo-continuum photometry spanning 42 wavelength bins across rest-frame 0.12--1.05 μm, and archival HST and millimeter interferometry data from NOEMA and PdBI. The integrated SED is dominated by star-heated dust, with only a marginal AGN contribution at galaxy-wide scales (f_ ^ =0.09 AGN int The nuclear core, however, requires a significant AGN component (f_ =0.34 AGN ) to account for a mid-infrared excess at rest-frame wavelengths of ∼2.5--3.6 μm characteristic of AGN-heated torus dust. The AGN accounts for sim34% of the nuclear infrared luminosity but only sim9% of the total integrated L_ spectroscopy. The inferred black hole mass places GN20 within the local M_ while its aperture-corrected luminosity is the same in the two apertures, explaining its weak signature in integrated diagnostics and its consistency with existing upper limits from Spitzer relation at the Eddington limit, and in the over-massive regime at sub-Eddington accretion rates, suggesting early and rapid black hole assembly concurrent with the dominant starburst. GN20 exemplifies a class of systems in which nuclear-scale SED decomposition, enabled by the angular resolution and infrared sensitivity of JWST, is the only means to uncover a buried AGN overwhelmed by galaxy-wide star formation.

title: Early identification of reversible strangulating ischemia in adhesive small bowel obstruction using non-contrast computed tomography and routine laboratory parameters
abstractText: BACKGROUND Early identification of reversible strangulating ischemia in patients with adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO) remains challenging. AIM To develop a preliminary predictive model for strangulating ischemia based on risk factors, non-contrast computed tomography (CT) findings, and routine laboratory parameters. METHODS This retrospective study included data from 103 patients with surgically confirmed ASBO. Patients were classified into two groups based on the ischemia type: Non-strangulating (n = 74) and strangulating ischemia (n = 29). Clinical variables, laboratory results, and CT features were analyzed using multivariate logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses. RESULTS Shorter symptom duration before admission [odds ratio (OR) = 0.972, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.953-0.992], mesenteric haziness (OR = 4.723, 95%CI: 1.099-20.294), closed-loop obstruction (OR = 7.181, 95%CI: 1.494-34.526), and lower base excess (OR = 0.604, 95%CI: 0.420-0.869) were independently associated with strangulating ischemia. The combined model yielded an area under the ROC curve of 0.897 (95%CI: 0.822-0.948), with a sensitivity of 82.76% and a specificity of 93.24%. CONCLUSION A preliminary model combining non-contrast CT findings and routine laboratory parameters helps identify strangulating ischemia at a potentially reversible stage of ASBO and supports early surgical decision-making.

title: Clinical application of personalized biodegradable anastomotic stent via preoperative intestinal three-dimensions reconstruction in laparoscopic resection of rectal cancer
abstractText: BACKGROUND Anastomotic complications affect postoperative recovery in patients with rectal cancer; therefore, more effective treatment strategies are urgently needed. AIM To analyze the clinical value of personalized biodegradable anastomotic reinforcement stents based on preoperative three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction parameters of the intestinal tract in laparoscopic anterior resection for rectal cancer. METHODS A total of 82 patients with rectal cancer who were admitted to our hospital between March 2023 and May 2025 were enrolled and divided into control and study groups according to the order of surgery. Both groups underwent laparoscopic anterior resection of the rectal cancer. The control group underwent conventional anastomosis, whereas the study group underwent implantation of personalized biodegradable anastomotic reinforcement stents based on the preoperative 3D reconstruction parameters of the intestinal tract. Perioperative indicators, postoperative recovery, anastomosis-related complications, postoperative inflammatory response levels and follow-up outcomes were compared between the two groups. RESULTS The stoma duration was longer in the study group than in the control group (P < 0.05). There were no significant differences in intraoperative blood loss, number of dissected lymph nodes, or conversion rate to open surgery between the two groups (P > 0.05). The time to first bowel sound recovery, time to first flatus, time to first oral intake, and time to first ambulation were shorter in the study group than in the control group (P < 0.05). The total incidence of anastomosis-related complications in the study group was 4.88% (2/41), which was lower than 21.95% (9/41) in the control group, with a significant difference (P < 0.05). The levels of inflammatory indicators at 1 day and 3 days after surgery in the study group were lower than those in the control group (P < 0.05). The Wexner incontinence and low anterior resection syndrome scores at 6 months and 12 months after surgery were significantly lower in the study group than in the control group (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION Implantation of personalized biodegradable anastomotic reinforcement stents based on preoperative 3D reconstruction parameters of the intestinal tract can promote postoperative intestinal function recovery, reduce the risk of anastomosis-related complications and inflammatory stimulation, and simultaneously improve postoperative defecation and anal function in patients undergoing laparoscopic anterior resection of rectal cancer.

title: Accretion-disk formation around orbiting stellar black holes in gaseous star clusters
abstractText: We consider low-mass black holes (BHs) moving in regular orbits in the cores of nonrotating gaseous star clusters representative of protostellar clusters or the centers of protogalaxies. We argue that as the BH's sphere of influence---the Bondi sphere---is advected along the BH trajectory, the transverse velocity shear between the inner and outer hemispheres injects angular momentum, driving the formation of an accretion disk. Coriolis forces oppose angular-momentum injection, delaying disk formation but not preventing it. The disk lies in the BH orbital plane and is counter-rotating with respect to the orbital BH motion. We verified this picture with 2D and 3D hydrodynamic simulations in the non-inertial frame of the orbiting BH. We find that the disk-formation timescale following a disruption event is on the order the Bondi crossing timescale, τ_ ̊m d ∼ R_ ̊m B /V_∙, and that the disk radius is on the order of R_ ̊m d ∼ ω_∙^2 R_ ̊m B ̊m M _⊙, inside the core of a typical compact protostellar cluster, these values read τ_ ̊m d ∼ 0.1 P_ ̊m orbit and R_ ̊m d ∼ 10^ -3 R_ ̊m B .

title: Construction and validation of a prognostic prediction model based on albumin-bilirubin grade after resection of hepatocellular carcinoma
abstractText: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the world's major health problems and high recurrence after curative resection limits long-term survival. Existing prognostic tools, such as Child-Pugh score, are limited by subjective aspects. Albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade (objective lab parameters) is shown to have an advantage in assessing liver function and prognosis. Given the limitations of existing prognostic tools and the proven prognostic value of ALBI grade in HCC, there is a need to develop an integrated, objective prediction model for postoperative recurrence risk stratification. AIM To construct and validate a prognostic prediction model based on ALBI grade after HCC resection. METHODS We looked back at clinical data from 596 patients with HCC who had a radical hepatectomy from 2021 to 2023. Using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, we identified independent predictors of recurrence-free survival (RFS). We then built a nomogram that combines these predictors to estimate 1- and 2-year RFS. RESULTS In the ALBI 2/3 group, the median RFS was 20.0 months. While the median RFS in the ALBI level 1 group was not reached at the end of the study, the differences between the two groups were statistically significant (P < 0.001). Multifactor Cox regression analysis showed that ALBI score, age, tumor size, tumor number, and alpha-fetoprotein levels were independent predictors of the effect on RFS (P < 0.05). We built nomogram with a consistency index (C-index) of 0.647 in the training set and 0.643 in the validation set. From the results of the time dependency analysis, area under the curve was 0.638-0.676 in the 1- and 2-year RFS predictions. CONCLUSION ALBI grade independently predicts HCC postoperative recurrence. Our integrated nomogram combining ALBI and clinical factors enables personalized recurrence risk stratification to guide individualized postoperative management.

title: Research progress on traditional Chinese medicine emotional nursing for drug efficacy and negative emotions in elderly post-gastrointestinal surgery patients
abstractText: With an accelerating aging population, the number of elderly patients undergoing gastrointestinal surgery is increasing annually. Postoperative pharmacotherapy efficacy and negative emotion management are critical factors that influence patient recovery outcomes. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) emotional nursing, centered on the theories of “unity of form and spirit” and “emotional factors contributing to disease”, plays a significant role in optimizing postoperative drug efficacy, alleviating anxiety and depression, and improving qi-blood circulation and visceral functions through targeted emotional regulation. This article systematically reviews the core theories of TCM emotional nursing and its application in elderly patients after gastrointestinal surgery, based on recent domestic and international research. It focuses on analyzing the synergistic effects of TCM emotional nursing on postoperative drug efficacy and interventions for negative emotions while exploring existing research limitations and future directions to provide a reference for clinical nursing practices and related studies in elderly patients undergoing gastrointestinal surgery.

title: Rectal granular cell tumor treated by endoscopic resection: A case report and review of literature
abstractText: BACKGROUND Granular cell tumors (GCTs) rarely occur in the gastrointestinal tract and are particularly uncommon in the rectum. We report a 34-year-old woman diagnosed with rectal GCT. In addition, we reviewed the published literature on rectal GCTs to summarize their clinical characteristics, diagnosis, and management. CASE SUMMARY The patient underwent a colonoscopy without any symptoms and no remarkable medical or family history of malignancy. A solitary 6-mm polypoid lesion was identified in the rectum and was resected endoscopically, with no additional lesions identified during colonoscopy. The patient had no complications after resection. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examinations confirmed the diagnosis of GCT. CONCLUSION The etiology, pathology, and biopsy diagnosis of GCT still require further research.

title: Time-dependent burden of reflux-related endoscopic pathology after sleeve gastrectomy: Clinical value of surveillance endoscopy in a 520-patient cohort
abstractText: BACKGROUND Sleeve gastrectomy is a widely performed procedure; however, postoperative gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux-related mucosal injury remain clinically persistent concerns. The value and timing of postoperative surveillance endoscopy are controversial, particularly because symptoms may not fully reflect mucosal pathology. AIM To evaluate time-dependent, reflux-related, clinical and endoscopic pathology after sleeve gastrectomy and to assess the clinical utility of postoperative surveillance endoscopy. METHODS This retrospective cohort study included adults who underwent sleeve gastrectomy and both pre- and postoperative upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. Among 560 patients screened, 520 were included in the final cohort; after excluding those with preoperative Barrett’s, 502 were eligible for de novo Barrett’s esophagus analysis. The primary endpoint was strict clinically significant postoperative endoscopic pathology, defined as Los Angeles grade B (LA-B) or higher erosive esophagitis, histology-confirmed Barrett’s, de novo Barrett’s, or esophageal stricture. A broader clinically actionable endpoint was analyzed separately. RESULTS The mean follow-up was 52.8 ± 20.9 months. GERD symptoms increased from 26.5% to 43.3%, proton pump inhibitor use increased from 22.5% to 50.6%, erosive esophagitis increased from 16.0% to 29.6%, LA-B or higher esophagitis increased from 5.8% to 13.1%, and Barrett’s increased from 3.5% to 10.0%. De novo Barrett’s esophagus occurred in 34/502 (6.8%) patients. Strict clinically significant pathology was present in 108/520 (20.8%) patients, and broader clinically actionable pathology was present in 198/520 (38.1%). Treatment changes occurred in 172/520 (33.1%) patients. CONCLUSION Reflux-related clinical/endoscopic findings increase after sleeve gastrectomy, especially at longer follow-up intervals, thus supporting risk-adapted endoscopic surveillance, particularly beyond 3-5 years, but do not establish requirements for annual endoscopy.

title: Enhanced recovery after surgery, based perioperative bundle reduces 30-day unplanned readmission after laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery
abstractText: BACKGROUND Laparoscopic resection has become standard for colorectal cancer (CRC) but postoperative recovery is often impaired by delayed gastrointestinal function, poor mobility and inadequate pain control resulting in increased risk of complications and unplanned readmission. Recovery is generally slower with conventional care, which follows conservative feeding and activity protocols. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathway combines several evidence-based perioperative interventions that reduce surgical stress and promote recovery, but there are no specific data regarding the effect of this program on 30-day unplanned readmission after laparoscopic colonoctol cancer surgery. This study was designed to compare an ERAS-based perioperative bundle with conventional care in terms of 30-day unplanned readmission and recovery outcomes. AIM To analyze the impact of ERAS pathway-based comprehensive perioperative management bundle on 30-day unplanned readmission rate after laparoscopic radical resection for CRC, and to evaluate its improvement effects on patients’ recovery-related indicators, functional recovery, and quality of life. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed 77 patients underwent laparoscopic radical resection for CRC in the Department of Gastrointestinal Surgery of our hospital from July 2020 to June 2021. Patients were divided based on the initiation time of rehabilitation treatment protocols: Control group (n = 38, conventional rehabilitation care) and intervention group (n = 39, ERAS pathway-based comprehensive perioperative management bundle). The intervention group received a combination of preoperative individualized rehabilitation education, postoperative early activity training, gastrointestinal function rehabilitation, multimodal analgesia, psychological support and discharge preparation with continuity of care as multilateral comprehensive managementiy. The unplanned 30-day readmission rate, recovery-related indicators, pain scores, functional recovery indicators, satisfaction with treatment and quality of life were compared between the groups. RESULTS The 30-day unplanned readmission rate in the intervention group (5.1%) was significantly lower than that recorded in controls (23.7%) (Fisher’s exact test, P = 0.024). Compared with the control group, time to first ambulation, first flatus, first defecation and recovery of gastrointestinal function in intervention group were shorter (all P < 0.001). Patients in the intervention group had significantly lower pain scores than those in the control group on postoperative days 1, 3, and 7 (all P < 0.001). In the intervention group, the 6-minute walk distance on postoperative day 7 was significantly greater than that in the control group (P < 0.001). Barthel Index scores at discharge and 30 days postoperatively in the intervention group were superior to those of the control group (P < 0.05). At 30 days postoperatively, the patient satisfaction scores in the intervention group were significantly higher than the controls (P < 0.001), and all dimensions of 36-item short-form health survey quality of life scale showed various degrees of improvement at 30-day after surgery (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION The ERAS pathway-based comprehensive perioperative management bundle can reduce the 30-day unplanned readmission rate after laparoscopic CRC surgery significantly, which in effectively promotes early postoperative recovery, pain control, functional recovery level and improves quality of life. In summary, the synergistic effects of each individual component are attributed to these clinical advantages because the intervention is a multi-component bundle and worthy of clinical perioperative care promotion and application.

title: Effects of modified ligation of intersphincteric fistula tract on intestinal barrier function in patients with transsphincteric anal fistula
abstractText: BACKGROUND The treatment for transsphincteric anal fistula (TAF) remains challenging. Effective therapies that achieve high efficacy and low recurrence while preserving anal sphincter function are still lacking. AIM To analyze the effects of modified ligation of intersphincteric fistula tract (LIFT) on infection-related parameters and intestinal barrier function in patients with TAF. METHODS A total of 101 patients with TAF admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University between January 2022 and June 2024 were retrospectively enrolled. Patients were grouped according to the treatment received: The control group (n = 49) underwent conventional anal fistulectomy, whereas the research group (n = 52) underwent modified LIFT. Clinical efficacy, surgical outcomes (e.g. , operation time, hospitalization, wound healing time, and postoperative scar area), anal sphincter function assessed using Wexner score, pain intensity assessed using Visual Analogue Scale, infection-related parameters, including white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin, intestinal barrier function, including diamine oxidase and D-lactic acid, complications, including anal canal deformity, anal edema, infection, constipation, and urinary retention), and the one-year recurrence rate were compared between groups. RESULTS Compared with the control group, the research group exhibited a significantly higher total effective rate, shorter operation time, hospitalization, and wound healing time, a smaller postoperative scar area, lower postoperative Wexner and Visual Analogue Scale scores, lower levels of infection-related parameters, and reduced overall complication and one-year recurrence rates. Postoperative intestinal barrier function indicators were comparable between groups. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that modified LIFT demonstrates reliable efficacy and safety in patients with TAF.

title: Impact of narrative therapy and standard ostomy care on postoperative recovery and complications in permanent colostomy
abstractText: BACKGROUND Permanent colostomy poses substantial physical and psychological challenges that impede postoperative recovery. AIM To evaluate whether adding narrative therapy (NT) to standard ostomy care (SOC) improves postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing permanent colostomy. METHODS This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent elective permanent colostomy from June 2022 to June 2025. Patients were divided into an NT combined with SOC (NTSOC) group and an SOC group on the basis of receipt of postoperative NT. Outcomes assessed included gastrointestinal recovery, early mobilization, hospital stay, self-care ability at 3 months, stoma complications within 3 months, psychosocial adaptation at 3 months, and stigma perception immediately postoperatively and at 3 months. RESULTS The baseline information of each group was comparable. The NTSOC group showed significantly faster gastrointestinal recovery (first oral rehydration: 48.24 hours vs 56.43 hours, P < 0.001) and earlier resumption of normal activities (3.31 days vs 3.75 days). The length of hospital stay was significantly shorter in the NTSOC group than in the SOC group (11.46 days vs 12.37 days, P = 0.016). By 3 months, the NTSOC group exhibited lower persisting concern than the SOC group (12.27 vs 13.75, P = 0.002). A significant difference was found in terms of accepting life (11.59 vs 10.36, P = 0.002); more optimistic attitude (17.44 vs 16.02, P = 0.001); and reduction in the stigmatized perception of social isolation, internalized shame, and perceived social exclusion. However, economic insecurity did not vary significantly (P = 0.091). CONCLUSION NTSOC is associated with accelerated recovery, fewer complications, enhanced self-care, better psychosocial adaptation, and reduced stigma in patients undergoing permanent colostomy.

title: Pattern Of Isolated Fungi from Bronchoalveolar Lavage Among Patients With Bronchial Asthma
abstractText: Background: Asthma is a long-standing inflammatory illness of the bronchial tree in which symptoms fluctuate over time while inflammation persists. Patients whose asthma is hard to treat or poorly controlled represent a major challenge in practice, because they experience a disproportionate number of exacerbations, make heavy use of health services and suffer a reduced quality of life. Accumulating data suggest that fungi colonizing or infecting the bronchi, chiefly Candida and Aspergillus species, can worsen the disease, probably through continuous bronchial inflammation, disordered immunity and a weaker response to therapy. Aim: This work set out to estimate how often fungi are recovered from bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid of adults whose bronchial asthma is uncontrolled or difficult to treat, to describe which fungi are found, and to relate these results to the clinical, laboratory and imaging profile of the patients. Patients and methods: Fifty-nine adult asthmatics attending Mansoura University Hospital (Chest Medicine Department) were enrolled in this prospective, cross-sectional work from May 2024 through May 2026. Every patient had experienced repeated exacerbations although treated according to guidelines. The work-up comprised clinical examination, spirometry with reversibility testing after salbutamol, CT of the chest, blood investigations and BAL. Lavage fluid was screened for fungal elements under the microscope and was also plated on Sabouraud dextrose agar. Each patient was then assigned to one of three groups (no fungal infection, probable fungal infection or fungal colonization) according to the semi-quantitative degree of growth and a modified version of the EORTC/MSG/SECURE criteria.

title: The detection of atrial fibrillation by implantable event recorders: A study of patients who have had a cryptogenic stroke
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Arial fibrillation (AF) plays a role in approximately one-third of ischemic strokes. In embolic strokes of undetermined source (ESUS), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation often escapes detection; if detected, it could be an indication for oral anticoagulation. In the ARTESiA trial, the absolute benefit of anticoagulation was higher in patients who had already had a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) than in those who had not. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from 233 consecutive ESUS patients at the Jena University Hospital who had received an implanted loop recorder (ILR) over the period 2021-2025. We additionally provide a narrative review on the detection rates associated with various monitoring strategies based on pertinent publications that were retrieved by a literature search. RESULTS: The 12-month detection rate of paroxysmal AF was 24.0% (56/233, 95% confidence interval [19.0; 29.9]). 73.2% of the initial detections were within the first 90 days. All patients in whom AF was detected were orally anticoagulated. The 12-month detection rate was higher than in the CRYSTAL-AF trial (12.4%) and the PER-DIEM trial (15.3%), but lower than was reported by Pikija et al. (31.3%). The cutoff values with the highest positive predictive value were a stroke risk analysis (SRA) index of 2 or above (38.4%) and age 75 or above (37.9%). CONCLUSION: Early, risk-adapted diagnostic testing with ILR in selected ESUS patients can detect clinically relevant AF. Advanced age and an elevated SRA index may be useful patient selection criteria. A robust number needed to treat (NNT) for the ILR strategy cannot be derived from the available one-armed registry data. The indication for ILR should be linked to its therapeutic relevance, the probability of detecting AF, and the individual hemorrhagic risk.

title: Effect of emergency integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine plus clinical nursing pathway in surgically-treated acute appendicitis patients
abstractText: BACKGROUND Given the high risk of postoperative complications in patients undergoing surgery for acute appendicitis (AA), optimizing management methods is critical. AIM To elucidate the effects of emergency integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine (ITCWM) combined with clinical nursing pathway (CNP) on surgical candidates for AA. METHODS A retrospective analysis was conducted on 130 individuals with AA requiring surgical intervention at Tianjin Nankai Hospital from September 2022 to September 2025. This cohort included 60 cases in the control group, which received routine nursing care, and 70 patients in the research group, who were treated with emergency ITCWM and CNP. Comparative analyses between the groups assessed several factors, including surgical recovery (time to bowel sound recovery, first flatus, ambulation, and length of hospital stay), postoperative pain (measured by the Numeric Rating Scale), mental state (Hamilton Depression/Anxiety Scale), sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index), and complications (ileus, uroschesis, incision infection). RESULTS The data revealed a significantly shorter time to bowel sound recovery, first flatus, and ambulation, along with earlier hospital discharge and lower Numeric Rating Scale scores on postoperative days 1 and 3 in the research group compared to controls. Reductions in Hamilton Depression Scale, Hamilton Anxiety Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores were noted on the 1st and 3rd postoperative days, alongside a lower total complication rate (7.14% vs 20.00%). CONCLUSION The integration of emergency ITCWM and CNP demonstrates substantial advantages for AA patients requiring surgery, indicating a strong potential for clinical application.

title: Colonoscope incarceration in an inguinal hernia complicated by ischemic bowel disease: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Colonoscopy is widely used for the diagnosis and treatment of colorectal diseases, with bleeding and perforation being the most recognized complications. Colonoscope incarceration within an inguinal hernia is an exceptionally rare mechanical complication, and secondary ischemic bowel injury has not been previously reported. CASE SUMMARY A 67-year-old man undergoing colonoscopy developed sudden complete fixation of the colonoscope at approximately 40 cm from the anal verge. Physical examination revealed a palpable mass in the left inguinal region. Pelvic X-ray demonstrated incarceration of the colonoscope in a characteristic reversed “S” configuration. Two-person manual reduction successfully released the scope. Subsequent colonoscopy showed continuous congestion, edema, and superficial necrosis of the sigmoid colon mucosa with clear demarcation from adjacent normal tissue. Histopathological examination confirmed ischemic mucosal injury. Computed tomography demonstrated a left inguinal hernia. The patient subsequently underwent elective hernia repair and recovered without further gastrointestinal complications. This case represents the first reported instance of ischemic bowel injury secondary to colonoscope incarceration within an inguinal hernia. Early recognition, prompt groin examination, imaging confirmation, coordinated manual reduction, and post-reduction mucosal assessment are essential for optimal management. CONCLUSION Routine pre-colonoscopy screening for inguinal hernia should be considered to prevent this rare but potentially severe complication.

title: Direct comparison of the effects of functionally equivalent dosing regimens of methamphetamine, methcathinone, and α-pyrrolidinopropiophenone on behavioral and neurochemical markers of stimulant-induced neurotoxicity
abstractText: Given that previous studies have provided mixed results on cathinone neurotoxicity, we compared the effects of 'functionally equivalent' dosing regimens of methamphetamine (METH), methcathinone, and α-pyrrolidinopropiophenone (α-PPP) on behavioral and neurochemical markers associated with dopaminergic alterations and cognitive function. Male Swiss Webster mice received METH (5 mg/kg), methcathinone (80 mg/kg), or α-PPP (80 mg/kg), using a 'binge'-like dosing regimen (q2h × 4, intraperitoneal). Body weight and temperature were recorded during dosing. Behavior was assessed 2-4 days later, followed by brain extraction. Motor function was evaluated by open-field testing and stride length analysis. Cognitive function was assessed with the passive avoidance test. Striatal levels of dopamine and its major metabolites were measured using ultra-HPLC. All three drug treatments induced weight loss. METH treatment produced a small, transient increase in rectal temperature (~1 °C); methcathinone and α-PPP did not. All three drug treatments impaired passive avoidance performance ( P < 0.05 to P < 0.01), but none produced persistent motor deficits. METH and methcathinone treatment significantly reduced striatal dopamine levels ( P < 0.001), whereas α-PPP did not, and only METH treatment increased homovanillic acid/dopamine turnover ( P < 0.01). Only METH exposure triggered measurable changes in dopamine metabolism and a small, transient increase in temperature, highlighting its distinct neurochemical profile compared with methcathinone and α-PPP under these conditions. All three drug treatments impaired passive avoidance performance, but none caused lasting motor deficits, demonstrating that behavioral deficits can occur without persistent motor changes.

title: Omeprazole-cisapride combination for gastroparesis following radical gastrectomy for gastric cancer: An efficacy and safety analysis
abstractText: BACKGROUND The management of gastroparesis (GP) following radical gastrectomy (RGE) for gastric cancer (GC) remains challenging, and treatment optimization is needed because current therapeutic approaches have limited efficacy. AIM To investigate the clinical efficacy and safety of omeprazole (OME) combined with cisapride (CIS) in the treatment of GP after RGE in patients with GC. METHODS A total of 198 patients with post-RGE GP were retrospectively enrolled from September 2020 to September 2025. Patients were grouped according to treatment regimen: 92 patients receiving OME constituted the control group, and 106 patients receiving OME plus CIS comprised the research group. Outcomes included clinical efficacy, symptom improvement assessed using the GP Cardinal Symptom Index, gastrointestinal function recovery (time to bowel sound recovery, nasogastric tube removal, and resumption of a normal diet), gastrointestinal hormone levels (gastrin and motilin), and safety (diarrhea, abdominal pain, headache/dizziness, palpitations, and nausea). Factors influencing treatment efficacy were subsequently evaluated. RESULTS The research group showed a significantly higher total effective rate than the control group. Following treatment, GP Cardinal Symptom Index scores across all domains were lower, the time to bowel sound recovery, nasogastric tube removal, and normal diet resumption was shorter, and gastrin and motilin levels were higher in patients receiving the combination therapy. The incidence of total adverse reactions was comparable between the two groups. Tumor-node-metastasis staging, baseline motilin level, and treatment regimen were independent factors affecting treatment efficacy. CONCLUSION OME combined with CIS is effective for treating GP after RGE for GC without increasing the overall incidence of adverse reactions. Additionally, stage IIB-III disease, baseline motilin < 309 mg/L, and treatment with OME alone are associated with an increased risk of treatment inefficacy.

title: Mechanisms, clinical translation, and future perspectives of liver-mediated immunoprotection in combined organ transplantation
abstractText: Owing to its unique tolerogenic immune microenvironment, the liver can confer substantial immunologic protection on concurrently transplanted allogeneic grafts in combined organ transplantation. This review summarizes the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying liver-mediated immunoprotection, including antigen presentation by liver sinusoidal endothelial cells and tolerogenic dendritic cells, enrichment of regulatory T cells, clonal deletion of donor-reactive T cells, clearance of donor-specific antibodies, and the establishment of microchimerism. We further synthesize clinical outcome data from combined liver-intestinal transplantation and multivisceral transplantation, and evaluate the translational potential of optimized immunosuppressive strategies, cell-based therapies, and emerging technologies such as normothermic machine perfusion. Although current evidence supports the immunoprotective role of the liver, its precise molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined and require further validation. Prospective multicenter studies are also warranted.

title: Prophylactic application of modified vacuum-assisted closure therapy in Ivor Lewis esophagectomy: Preliminary results
abstractText: BACKGROUND Ivor Lewis esophagectomy is the standard surgical approach for middle and distal esophageal cancer. Despite advances in minimally invasive techniques and perioperative care, anastomotic leakage (AL) remains a major cause of postoperative morbidity and mortality. Although prophylactic endoluminal vacuum therapy has shown promise, its clinical use is limited by procedural complexity and cost. AIM To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical outcomes of a modified, endoscopy-independent prophylactic vacuum-assisted closure system (ModVAC) in patients undergoing Ivor Lewis esophagectomy. METHODS This retrospective single-center study included 31 patients who underwent Ivor Lewis esophagectomy from July 2019 to June 2024. Sixteen patients received prophylactic ModVAC therapy, while fifteen earlier patients served as historical controls. The primary outcome was AL. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. AL occurred in 25% vs 40% of patients (P = 0.37), with all ModVAC leaks managed non-operatively. Hospital stay, morbidity, and mortality were similar. Protocol completion was 81.25% with minimal device-related complications. CONCLUSION Prophylactic ModVAC is a feasible and safe adjunct following Ivor Lewis esophagectomy. Although leak reduction was not statistically significant, the favorable management of leaks suggests potential clinical benefit. Larger prospective randomized studies are warranted.

title: Development and validation of a postoperative prediction model for residual stones after hepatectomy in patients with hepatolithiasis
abstractText: BACKGROUND Residual stones after hepatectomy for hepatolithiasis are associated with recurrent cholangitis, repeat interventions, and long-term biliary morbidity. Current classification systems assist in disease characterization and operative planning but fail to provide individualized risk estimates in the early postoperative period. AIM To develop and internally validate an early postoperative model for predicting residual stones in patients with hepatolithiasis after hepatectomy. METHODS This study included 300 consecutive patients who underwent hepatectomy between January 2019 and December 2022. Residual stones were identified by postoperative imaging within 1 year and classified as incomplete clearance rather than recurrence. The cohort was randomly split into a development dataset (70%) and a held-out internal validation dataset (30%), and 12 candidate prediction models were developed and compared. Within the development dataset, preprocessing, feature shrinkage, hyperparameter tuning, and algorithm selection were performed using repeated nested cross-validation (outer 5-fold cross-validation repeated three times; inner 5-fold cross-validation). The final model was then locked and evaluated in the held-out validation cohort. Model performance was evaluated based on discrimination, prediction error, calibration, threshold-based classification, and decision-curve analysis. RESULTS Residual stones were identified in 82 of 300 patients (27.3%). The development cohort included 211 patients (58 events), and the validation cohort included 89 patients (24 events). Based solely on the out-of-fold performance within the development cohort, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-penalized logistic regression (LASSO-LR) was selected as the final model. This model achieved a patient-level out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.849 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.794-0.904] and a Brier score of 0.138. In the validation cohort, the AUC was 0.877 (95%CI: 0.807-0.947) with a Brier score of 0.134, confirming stable discrimination and predictive accuracy. Using the development-derived cutoff of 0.270, the validation sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value were 0.875, 0.785, and 0.944, respectively. The final model retained four predictors: Operative time, bilateral stone distribution, T-tube drainage, and postoperative biliary stricture before outcome ascertainment. Calibration intercepts neared zero in both cohorts, and decision-curve analysis showed net benefit across threshold probabilities from 0.05 to 0.40. CONCLUSION The LASSO-LR model demonstrated favorable internally validated performance for early postoperative residual-stone risk stratification and may facilitate individualized surveillance after hepatectomy for hepatolithiasis.
