title: Improving constraints on the Yukawa correction at the Galactic center with multiple stellar orbits
abstractText: We investigate the presence of a Yukawa-like correction (∝ , α - r/łambda ) to Newtonian gravity at the Galactic center, using a multi-star fitting code, including the newly discovered star S301, to improve the constraints obtained using S2 orbit alone. We performed a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis using the astrometric and spectroscopic data of stars S2, S55, S29, S38, and S301 collected by GRAVITY, GRAVITY+$, NACO, and SINFONI instruments, covering the period from 1992 to $2025. Compared to our previous paper, in which only S2 was fitted, the tightest bound on the Yukawa coupling is again reached at łambda = 3̧dot10^ 13 ,̊m m (∼ 200,AU), where we find $|α| < 6 -4 $, an improvement of roughly a factor of 5. The addition of S301 extends the constraint to short ranges that were inaccessible to S2, yielding $|α| < 0.004$ at łambda =10^ 12 ,̊m m and $|α| < 0.006$ at łambda =5⋅ 10^ 11 ,̊m m. By contrast, S29, with its larger apoapsis, yields $|α| < 0.1$ at łambda ∼ 2̧dot10^ 15 ,̊m m. The latter two represent the tightest limits at these scale lengths on a Yukawa correction obtained to date around a supermassive black hole.

title: Gastric metastasis from renal cell carcinoma with a 10-year interval: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Gastric metastasis of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is rare clinically, often presenting with a prolonged interval (median 7-10 years) between initial diagnosis and metastasis, rendering it prone to imaging oversight. CASE SUMMARY We report a 70-year-old man with advanced clear cell RCC (ccRCC) who developed gastric metastasis 10 years after initial radical nephrectomy. After adjuvant therapy with interleukin-2 and treatment of subsequent recurrent left renal pelvis RCC with partial nephrectomy and pazopanib, the patient received penpulimab plus axitinib for metastatic disease. A gastric fundus mass was detected by positron emission tomography/computed tomography during routine follow-up and confirmed as metastatic ccRCC by endoscopic biopsy and immunohistochemistry (PAX-8+, CA IX+, CD10+, CK7-). The patient underwent robot-assisted wedge resection of the stomach in August 2025 and remains on sintilimab maintenance immunotherapy. CONCLUSION For advanced RCC, gastric metastasis should remain part of differential diagnosis even in the absence of gastrointestinal symptoms.

title: Translational artificial intelligence in therapeutic-era metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: The ACTION framework
abstractText: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) has entered a therapeutic era in which priorities extend beyond detecting steatosis to identifying treatment-actionable fibrosis, rationalising referral and biopsy, standardising trial endpoints and monitoring response. Artificial intelligence (AI) spans electronic health records, non-invasive tests, imaging and digital pathology, but reports often omit the user, threshold and consequence. We conducted a structured narrative review and developed the author-proposed ACTION framework. ACTION comprises attached action, calibration in context, threshold-specific benefit, integration, oversight, and non-discrimination and monitoring. Evidence is uneven. Case-finding and enrichment models can identify uncoded or higher-risk patients, but their prospective effects on testing, referral and outcomes remain unproven. Imaging AI supports reproducible quantification, although signals may add little beyond clinical variables. The human-reviewed AI-based measurement tool for MASH (in regulatory records) is among the most mature applications reviewed, within a narrowly specified clinical-trial context. It is qualified for specified MASH clinical-trial workflows, not for autonomous diagnosis or unrestricted treatment selection. AI becomes clinically meaningful only when a calibrated output is linked to a predefined action, an accountable human user and a measurable patient or trial outcome.

title: Connecting the little dots in polarized light
abstractText: Recent observations of the local little red dot (LRD) analog SDSS J1025+1402 have revealed that the optical continuum is polarized at the sim1.5% level, while broad Hα has lower polarization (sim0.7%) and a different polarization angle. We investigate whether these properties can be reproduced in a scenario in which LRDs are dust-obscured little blue dots (LBDs) viewed at a high inclination and powered by super-Eddington accretion. In this framework, electron scattering in the geometrically thick inner accretion flow produces intrinsic continuum polarization, while unpolarized emission from the outer thin disk dilutes the signal, particularly at optical wavelengths. Broad Hα, which is emitted outside the compact disk atmosphere, lacks this intrinsic disk-atmosphere polarization. A circumnuclear dust screen then contributes dichroic polarization to both the continuum and broad-line emission, producing the lower line polarization and its distinct position angle. We show that this model reproduces the main observed polarization properties, although degeneracies between accretion rate and inclination remain. The standard polarization models we tested, based on equatorial and/or polar scattering in active galactic nuclei, fail to reproduce the observed continuum and broad-line polarization simultaneously. These results illustrate the potential of spectropolarimetry as a probe of accretion-flow geometry and orientation in the little-dot population, complementary to spectral-energy-distribution fitting and line diagnostics.

title: Incision and drainage vs minimally invasive catheter drainage on pain and anal function in high perianal abscess patients
abstractText: BACKGROUND Perianal abscess (PA) is a common and debilitating condition that requires prompt surgical intervention. Conventional incision and drainage, while standard, often results in significant postoperative pain, tissue trauma, and potential impairment of anal sphincter function, prompting the need for alternative approaches. AIM To compare the effect of incision and drainage with selective seton placement (ID) vs minimally invasive catheter drainage (MICD) on postoperative pain control and anal function preservation in patients with high PA. METHODS This retrospective study included 226 patients with high PA (defined as abscesses located above the levator ani muscle, confirmed by imaging) who underwent ID (n = 122) or MICD (n = 104). Primary outcomes were pain intensity identified using the visual analogue scale (preoperatively and on postoperative days 1, 7, and 14) and anal function according to Wexner score on postoperative day 30. Secondary outcomes included inflammatory cytokine levels [interleukin (IL)-4, IL-6, IL-10, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha], operative time, blood loss, wound healing time, and hospital stay. Anal fistula formation and abscess recurrence were evaluated as exploratory endpoints. RESULTS The MICD group demonstrated significantly lower visual analogue scale at all postoperative time points (all P < 0.001). A significantly higher proportion of patients in the MICD group achieved normal anal function (69.2% vs 48.4%, P = 0.002). On postoperative day 7, the MICD group showed lower levels of IL-4, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha and higher levels of IL-10 (all P < 0.01). Operative time, blood loss, wound healing, and hospital stay were significantly reduced in the MICD group (all P < 0.01). Exploratory analysis showed a lower rate of anal fistula formation (8.7% vs 24.6%, P = 0.002) and abscess recurrence (3.8% vs 12.3%, P = 0.023) with MICD. However, these findings are limited by inherent differences in internal opening management between the techniques. Multivariate analysis identified MICD as a protective factor against anal incontinence (odds ratio = 0.334, P = 0.003), whereas diabetes and deep abscess were risk factors (both P < 0.01). CONCLUSION MICD is associated with better postoperative pain control, better preservation of anal sphincter function, a more favorable anti-inflammatory response, and faster recovery than conventional ID in patients with high PA. The potential benefit regarding fistula risk reduction requires further validation in prospective studies with standardized internal opening protocols.

title: Trends, geographic variation and factors associated with the double burden of malnutrition among mother–child dyads in Nigeria: evidence from the pooled 2013, 2018 and 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Surveys
abstractText: Background Dyad-level double burden of malnutrition (DBM) — maternal overweight/obesity with stunting in her own child — reflects Nigeria’s nutrition transition, but national evidence comes from a single survey round. We examined the prevalence, components, trends, geographic variation and correlates of dyad-level DBM across three Nigeria Demographic and Health Surveys (NDHS). Methods We pooled Kids Recode data from the 2013, 2018 and 2024 NDHS. The analytic sample comprised 36,828 dyads of a living child aged 0–59 months with a valid height-for-age z-score (HAZ) and a mother with valid body mass index (BMI) who was neither pregnant nor within two months postpartum. DBM was defined as maternal BMI ≥ 25 kg/m² and child HAZ < − 2 SD. Survey-weighted logistic regression with round-specific strata and clusters estimated odds ratios, and three-level random-intercept models partitioned variation between clusters and states. Results DBM prevalence was 6.26% (95% CI 5.78–6.77) in 2013, 6.78% (6.08–7.55) in 2018 and 5.28% (4.63–6.03) in 2024 (p = 0.017); pooled prevalence (6.18%) was about two-thirds of that expected if the two conditions were independent. Odds were lower in 2024 than in 2013 after adjustment (AOR 0.83; 0.70–0.98). Higher adjusted odds were observed for children aged 12–59 months, mothers aged 35–49 years (AOR 1.67; 1.28–2.17), higher birth order, primary education (AOR 1.29; 1.08–1.54) and richer (AOR 2.36; 1.88–2.96) and richest households (AOR 2.28; 1.74–2.98); girls had lower odds (AOR 0.85; 0.76–0.94). Unadjusted regional differences were not significant (p = 0.241); after adjustment, the three southern regions had lower odds. Clusters and states together accounted for 17% of the latent variance (cluster median odds ratio 2.14) and states alone for about 1% (1.23). Conclusions About one in 16 mother–child dyads had DBM, with lower prevalence in 2024. DBM was more common in wealthier households and varied mainly between communities rather than states. Because overweight mothers were less likely than others to have a stunted child, maternal overweight and child stunting should be addressed as related but distinct problems across the wealth spectrum.

title: Enhanced recovery after surgery in colorectal surgery: Do average benefits mask heterogeneous effects in patients underrepresented in trials?
abstractText: For elective colorectal surgery, enhanced recovery protocols are now standard practice, with convincing trial evidence showing fewer complications and shorter stays. What we know far less about is whether that same evidence reliably applies to the patients who were routinely excluded from those trials, older frail adults, those with severe obesity, and people carrying multiple chronic conditions. Three observations from the available data give reason for caution. First, baseline physiological vulnerability predicts complications irrespective of protocol fidelity, a finding that suggests the benefit of compliance is not uniform across patient groups. Second, patients least likely to meet trial eligibility complete fewer elements of the protocol; whether such shortfalls reflect sound clinical judgement or inadvertent undertreatment has not been established. Third, socioeconomic disadvantage and ethnic minority background are linked to wider adherence gaps and poorer outcomes, even where institutional compliance appears high. These signals converge on a single gap in measurement. Existing audit systems document whether a protocol step was carried out, but not why it was omitted. A framework that fails to account for why protocol steps are omitted cannot distinguish clinical adaptation from neglect. Building that distinction into perioperative audit may matter as much for the patients at the margins of evidence as achieving higher compliance scores does for the average patient.

title: Impact of perioperative Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy on long-term survival after distal gastrectomy for gastric cancer
abstractText: BACKGROUND Persistent Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ) infection is associated with adverse outcomes after gastrectomy for gastric cancer. AIM To evaluate the association of perioperative H. pylori eradication therapy with longterm survival in patients undergoing distal gastrectomy for gastric cancer. METHODS This retrospective cohort study involved H. pylori -positive patients who underwent distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy for gastric adenocarcinoma at our hospital from January 2016 to January 2021. The patients were divided into a perioperative eradication group and a non-eradication group depending on whether they received a 14-day bismuth-containing quadruple regimen. Key measurements included H. pylori status at 6 months, nutritional/inflammatory parameters at 12 months, remnant gastric lesions at 1 year, adjuvant chemotherapy completion, and long-term oncologic outcomes, including 5-year overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS Among the 271 eligible patients (143 non-eradication and 128 eradication), the eradication success rate was 91.41% in the eradication group. Compared with the non-eradication group, the eradication group was associated with significantly higher 5-year OS (91.41% vs 80.42%, P = 0.010) and 5-year DFS (85.94% vs 72.73%, P = 0.008) and lower rates of metachronous gastric cancer (1.56% vs 7.69%, P = 0.018) and gastric cancer-specific death (6.25% vs 15.38%, P = 0.017). Multivariate Cox regression analysis adjusting for age, sex, pathological tumor-node-metastasis stage, differentiation, and lymphovascular invasion revealed that perioperative eradication remained independently associated with improved OS (hazard ratio = 0.551, P = 0.036) and DFS (hazard ratio = 0.604, P = 0.043). CONCLUSION In this retrospective cohort, perioperative H. pylori eradication therapy was independently associated with improved long-term survival and reduced risk of metachronous gastric cancer in patients who underwent distal gastrectomy for gastric cancer.

title: Epigenetic-immune landscape of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: From tumor biology to multimodal treatment in the surgical setting
abstractText: Pancreatic cancer, one of the most lethal malignancies, is characterized by aggressive progression, late diagnosis, and resistance to conventional therapies. Increasing evidence indicates that epigenetic alterations contribute not only to tumor progression but also to immune regulation. These epigenetic alterations regulate immune cell differentiation, infiltration, and function, thereby promoting the formation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This narrative minireview aims to summarize the current understanding of epigenetic-immune crosstalk in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and discuss its potential implications for translational research and future therapeutic development. Various epigenetic-immune interactions regulate immune checkpoints, macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and regulatory T cells, collectively contributing to immune evasion. Combinations of epigenetic modulators and immune checkpoint inhibitors are emerging, particularly in the surgical setting. They hold promise for restoring anti-tumor immunity and overcoming resistance. This article provides an overview of epigenetic-immune crosstalk in pancreatic cancer, with implications for novel therapies in the surgical setting. However, current evidence remains predominantly preclinical, and prospective studies are warranted.

title: Non-cirrhotic hyperammonemia in adults: Recognition and management
abstractText: In adults, an elevated ammonia level is almost reflexively attributed to cirrhosis. Yet hyperammonemia also occurs in patients with structurally normal livers, in whom the underlying cause is often missed. This delay matters because hyperammonemic brain injury depends on both the magnitude and duration of ammonia elevation. This review organizes the non-cirrhotic causes by mechanism. Ammonia production increases with urease-producing urinary tract infections, Ureaplasma or Mycoplasma infection after lung transplantation, heavy nitrogen loads, malignancy and chemotherapy, and urinary diversion. Clearance is impaired in adult-onset urea cycle disorders, with drugs such as valproate, post-gastric bypass, and when portal blood bypasses the liver through a portosystemic shunt. We outline a practical diagnostic approach: Confirm a true elevation using a properly handled sample, exclude cirrhosis, then use targeted testing, including plasma amino acids, urine orotic acid, acid-base assessment, acylcarnitine and zinc levels, and Doppler or cross-sectional imaging, to distinguish among these mechanisms. Management proceeds on two tracks: Lowering ammonia while simultaneously treating the underlying cause, which can be curative in several conditions. Early measurement of ammonia in patients with unexplained encephalopathy and normal liver tests can prevent avoidable neurologic injury.

title: Acquired hemophilia A following choledochal cyst excision - highlighting postoperative bile leak and infection as potential triggers: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Acquired hemophilia A (AHA) is a rare and potentially fatal bleeding disorder mediated by autoantibodies against coagulation factor VIII (FVIII). Its nonspecific clinical presentation often leads to delayed diagnosis and life-threatening complications. Early recognition and standardized management are crucial for improving outcomes. Secondary AHA following choledochal cyst excision is extremely rare, with no prior reports in the literature. This case report explored the possible etiology, treatment strategies, and disease course of AHA in a patient. CASE SUMMARY A 37-year-old woman developed postoperative bile leakage, infection, and recurrent bleeding after laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision with Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy, which was subsequently complicated by AHA. On postoperative day 6, she presented with intra-abdominal hemorrhage. Despite repeated interventions, including exploratory laparotomy and interventional embolization, intermittent active bleeding remained uncontrolled. After multidisciplinary team consultation, she was finally diagnosed with AHA. Treatment included infection control, combined immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide, seven plasma exchange sessions, and FVIII replacement therapy. Bleeding was effectively controlled, the intra-abdominal abscess healed, and the patient was discharged after clinical remission was achieved. At the 6-month follow-up, no signs of recurrent bleeding were noted. CONCLUSION Prompt FVIII activity and inhibitor testing, along with comprehensive treatment, should be implemented in patients suspicious for AHA.

title: Immunological patterns and clinical forms of primary biliary cholangitis
abstractText: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic, slowly progressive autoimmune liver disease of unknown etiology, characterized by the presence of antimitochondrial antibodies (AMA) and/or PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies, nonsuppurative destructive cholangitis and, in most cases, cholestasis, which in its natural course leads to biliary cirrhosis. PBC is considered a rare disease predominantly affecting middle-aged women. However, a significant rise in the incidence and prevalence of PBC has been observed worldwide recently, especially among men and younger individuals. In addition to “classic” PBC (AMA-positive with cholestasis), there are several special variants of the disease: AMA-negative PBC (without AMA with the presence of other markers or completely seronegative), variant syndromes such as PBC with features of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) or with features of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), and AMA-positive PBC without cholestatic syndrome (most likely a preclinical stage of the disease). These forms have clinical and laboratory differences and distinct autoantibody profiles. Some variants may have a more severe course and worse clinical outcomes. Studying the prevalence and clarifying the clinical and laboratory features of these special forms of PBC is of substantial scientific and practical importance for assessing disease prognosis, development of new approaches to its diagnosis and treatment. Early recognition of these variants remains a challenge. For the well-characterized forms - in particular PBC-AIH variant syndrome - timely, form-appropriate therapy is associated with slower progression and better transplant-free survival. For the less well-defined categories, including AMA-positive individuals without cholestasis, completely seronegative PBC and the PBC-PSC variant, a comparable benefit is plausible but has not been demonstrated prospectively. This article is a narrative review supported by a structured search of PubMed, EMBASE and Google Scholar covering 2005-2025, from which 101 studies were included, with a further 28 sources identified by citation tracking and hand-searching; no formal risk-of-bias appraisal, evidence grading or meta-analysis was performed. The six-form classification and the diagnostic algorithm presented here are the authors’ hypothesis-generating proposal, not validated or guideline-endorsed entities, and require prospective external validation.

title: Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis mimicking gallbladder carcinoma
abstractText: Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis (XGC) is a rare benign inflammatory disorder that can closely resemble gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) clinically, radiologically, intraoperatively, and even on gross pathological examination. This overlap may lead to both unnecessary radical surgery and undertreatment of unsuspected malignancy. This review summarizes the contemporary literature together with institutional clinical and radiological experience, focusing on diagnostic pitfalls and practical surgical decision-making. Two illustrative cases are also presented. Reliable preoperative differentiation between XGC and GBC remains difficult because symptoms, laboratory findings, tumor markers, and individual imaging features overlap considerably. A pattern-based interpretation of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging findings may improve diagnostic confidence. Diffuse wall thickening, continuous mucosal enhancement, intramural hypoattenuating or T2-hyperintense nodules, gallstones, and preservation of the mural architecture tend to favor XGC, whereas focal mass formation, mucosal disruption, biliary obstruction, lymphadenopathy, and convincing hepatic invasion raise greater concern for GBC. Machine-learning and deep-learning models have shown promising diagnostic performance, although external validation and improved interpretability are still required before they can be incorporated into routine clinical practice. Frozen-section analysis, careful nodal assessment, and delayed oncologic resection after definitive histological assessment when uncertainty persists may provide a reasonable balance between avoiding unnecessary radical procedures and preventing undertreatment of true malignancy.

title: Beyond station 16: A pathway-aware framework for gallbladder cancer lymphadenectomy after neoadjuvant therapy
abstractText: Gallbladder cancer is an aggressive biliary tract malignancy and lymph node status is among the strongest determinants of outcome. For decades, the surgical debate has focused on the extent of lymphadenectomy and on whether para-aortic or interaortocaval nodal involvement should be regarded as regional extension or systemic disease. This binary framing is useful for staging but anatomically incomplete. Classical lymphatic studies described three drainage routes: cholecysto-celiac, cholecysto-retropancreatic and cholecysto-mesenteric. These pathways involve stations 12, 8, 9, 13, 17 and 14 before converging toward station 16, especially 16a2 and 16b1. Current Western algorithms often focus on the hepatoduodenal ligament and treat para-aortic/interaortocaval nodal disease as a contraindication to curative-intent surgery. This Opinion Review proposes a pathway-aware framework for interpreting lymphadenectomy after neoadjuvant therapy. The concept is hypothesis-generating, not a validated therapeutic recommendation. For staging, reporting and research purposes, nodal assessment may be described by both nodal yield and station distribution; a six-node harvest limited to station 12 provides different anatomical information from a six-node harvest sampled across celiac, retropancreatic, mesenteric and para-aortic convergence basins. We do not advocate indiscriminate extended lymphadenectomy. Rather, in medically fit patients with adequate physiological reserve, no systemic progression and realistic R0 resection, pathway mapping and selective clearance may be discussed as an expert-center investigational framework. The key question is whether the involved pathway remains surgically controllable after biological selection, not simply whether station 16 is regional or metastatic.

title: Relationship between triglyceride glucose-related indices and risk of peripheral artery disease in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease participants
abstractText: BACKGROUND The association between triglyceride glucose (TyG)-related indices and risk of peripheral artery disease (PAD) in adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify the relationship between TyG-related indices [TyG, TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), TyG-waist circumference (TyG-WC), and TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR)] and PAD risk in MASLD, and compare predictive accuracy among these indices in predicting PAD risk. AIM To investigate the associations of TyG-related indices with PAD risk in patients with MASLD, and to compare the predictive performance of different TyG-derived indices for PAD risk in this population. METHODS In this prospective cohort study, participants with baseline MASLD and free of PAD were included. We used multivariable Cox models to assess the relationship between TyG-related indices (grouped by tertiles) and PAD risk, and population attributable fractions (PAF) to quantify the impact of TyG-related indices on PAD. We analyzed relative importance of TyG-related indices and other traditional cardiometabolic risk factors in predicting PAD. Predictive accuracy of TyG-related indices was compared using Harrell’s C-index, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. RESULTS A total of 163425 participants with MASLD at baseline were included for analysis (mean age: 57.26 years; 36.14% females). During follow-up, 3643 (2.23%) incident PAD events occurred. Compared with Tertile 1, Tertile 3 group was associated with significantly higher risk of PAD: TyG [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.20, 95%CI: 1.05-1.38], TyG-BMI (HR = 1.15, 95%CI: 1.00-1.33), TyG-WC (HR = 1.43, 95%CI: 1.23-1.65), and TyG-WHtR (HR = 1.31, 95%CI: 1.19-1.44). Tertile 3 and combination group (Tertile 2/3) had PAFs ranging from 8%-16%, when taking Tertile 1 as reference. TyG-related indices ranked only lower than smoking or low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in predicting PAD. Models adding TyG-WC or TyG-WHtR had highest improved model accuracy among the four indices. CONCLUSION TyG-related indices were significantly associated with PAD risk in the MASLD population, and incorporating TyG-related indices significantly improved model accuracy for predicting PAD risk. TyG-related indices may serve as adjunct markers for PAD risk stratification in MASLD populations, though further external validation is needed to confirm their clinical utility.

title: Liver disorders in pregnancy: An evidence-based guide to diagnosis and management
abstractText: Liver diseases complicate approximately 3% of pregnancies. Liver disorders that are unique to pregnancy include hyperemesis gravidarum, intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, hemolysis with elevated liver enzymes and low platelets syndrome and acute fatty liver of pregnancy. Additionally, certain acute and chronic liver diseases like viral hepatitis, autoimmune hepatitis, Wilson’s disease, vascular liver disorders and cirrhosis with portal hypertension may occur coincidentally during pregnancy. In addition, pregnancy induces physiological changes in liver function and in hepatic blood flow and metabolism, resulting in alterations of clinical presentation and management decisions. Their importance lies in significant maternal, fetal and neonatal morbidity and mortality. In conclusion, liver diseases in pregnancy require timely recognition, accurate diagnosis, multidisciplinary care (including obstetrician, hepatologist, and critical-care specialist), and judicious timing of delivery to optimise maternal and fetal outcomes. This article reviews current knowledge on the clinical manifestations, diagnostic approach, management, and outcomes of liver diseases in pregnancy, with special emphasis on gestational liver disorders.

title: Associations of individual exposure to particulate matter with next-day physical activity and sedentary behaviour in older adults: a micro-longitudinal study
abstractText: Background Staying physically active is essential for healthy ageing. Exposure to high levels of air pollutants such as particulate matter (PM) is associated with less active, more sedentary lifestyles in older adults. Whether results extend to typical fluctuations in daily PM exposure is unclear. We examined associations of higher-than-usual personal exposure to PM (PM 2.5 and PM 10) with next-day movement behaviour in older adults, assessed using concurrently worn personal air quality monitors and accelerometers. Methods The present study used 304 days of data from 67 adults aged 50–85 years living in the UK. For five days, participants wore accelerometers 24-h per day and personal air quality monitors during waking hours. Average daily time spent in movement behaviours (moderate-to-vigorous physical activity [MVPA], light physical activity [LPA], sedentary behaviour [SB]) and step count was extracted from accelerometers, and average daily exposure to PM 2.5 from personal air quality monitors. PM 10 was examined in secondary exploratory analyses. We used linear mixed models to examine within-person associations of deviation from usual PM exposure with next-day movement outcomes, with estimates presented for ‘usual’ (individual mean) and ‘higher-than-usual’ (+ 1 interquartile range, equivalent to 2.6 μg/m 3 beyond individual mean PM 2.5 exposure and 2.8 μg/m 3 beyond individual mean PM 10 exposure) exposure. Analyses were repeated using area-based PM estimates. Results Compared with usual exposure, higher-than-usual PM 2.5 was associated with 8 min less LPA (95% CI =− 14 to − 2) and 483 fewer steps (− 884 to − 82) on the following day. Exposure to higher-than-​​usual PM 10 was associated with 8 min less LPA (− 13 to − 3), 8 min more SB (0 to 15), and 412 fewer steps (− 739 to − 85) on the following day. There was no association with MVPA, and no associations when area-level PM estimates were used as opposed to estimates from personal air quality monitors. Conclusions Typical daily variability in PM exposure in a setting with relatively low overall PM levels was associated with modest next-day differences in movement behaviour in older adults. Higher-than-usual PM exposure was associated with less next-day activity and more sedentary time. Personal monitoring may be important for capturing short-term exposure-behaviour associations.

title: Intraoperative frozen section diagnosis of primary alpha-fetoprotein–positive hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder: A case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND This study explored the key points of intraoperative frozen pathological diagnosis and the clinical diagnostic value of primary alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)-positive hepatoid adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder (HAGB). CASE SUMMARY The clinical data, imaging findings, intraoperative frozen pathology, postoperative routine pathology, and immunohistochemical findings of a 61-year-old patient with AFP-HAGB admitted in 2023 were analyzed. Relevant literature was also reviewed. The patient was admitted because of a gallbladder mass detected during a physical examination, with significantly elevated serum AFP. The intraoperative frozen section showed typical hepatoid differentiation of the tumor, suggesting HAGB. Postoperative pathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed AFP-HAGB accompanied by lymph node metastasis. The patient’s condition stabilized after surgical treatment. CONCLUSION Intraoperative frozen pathology can rapidly and accurately identify AFP-HAGB. Combined with serum AFP, imaging, and immunohistochemistry, a clear diagnosis can be made, which is of significant clinical importance for guiding surgical decisions and reducing misdiagnosis.

title: The diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up management of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is a life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy. The global incidence of immune-mediated TTP (iTTP) is 1-6 cases per million people per year. The new (S3-level) clinical practice guideline is the first in the German-speaking world to compile evidence- and consensus-based recommendations on the diagnosis, treatment, follow-up management, and care of patients with immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) and congenital thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (cTTP). METHODS: This clinical practice guideline was developed under the aegis of the Society for Thrombosis and Hemostatsis Research (Gesellschaft für Thrombose- und Hämostaseforschung, GTH) according to the criteria for S3-level guidelines issued by the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF). It is based on information from publications retrieved through systematic literature searches and a structured assessment of the evidence using the GRADE scheme (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation), with a formal consensus process. RESULTS: Early diagnosis of TTP is essential. Measurement of ADAMTS13 activity is the diagnostic gold standard. In case of clinical suspicion of acute iTTP, treatment with plasma exchange, corticosteroids, and caplacizumab should be initiated at once. In a randomized trial with an active control group, plasma exchange lowered mortality at the end of the first treatment cycle from 15.7% to 3.9%. In a cohort study, standard treatment with plasma exchange, corticosteroids, caplacizumab, and rituximab was associated with a mortality of 2.2%, compared to 12.2% in a historical control cohort. Further management consists of regular clinical follow-up, ADAMTS13 monitoring, and the detection and treatment of late sequelae. For pregnancy in female TTP patients, monitoring and recurrence prophylaxis are recommended. CONCLUSION: The purpose of the clinical practice guideline is to improve the acute care and interdisciplinary management of TTP. Further research is needed on the use of recombinant ADAMTS13 and on the definition of uTTP (TTP in the absence of causative antibodies or genetic mutations).

title: Large language models as diagnostic tools in nephrology: Helpful, with limitations
abstractText: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to support diagnostic decision-making. It is unclear, however, whether their performance on knowledge and examination tasks translates to interpreting clinical case vignettes, especially when a complete diagnosis requires specifying several related elements, such as triggers, organ manifestations, or complications. METHODS: We carried out a vignette-based benchmark study using 101 case reports from the German-language journal Die Nephrologie to assess six current language models from the Anthropic, Google, and Open AI companies. The strongest model of each company as of March 2026 was tested, as well as one smaller model from each. The models were required to provide a differential diagnosis with five disease entities and to name the most likely diagnosis. The answers were evaluated using a three-level scale. We drew a distinction between diagnoses with a single component and diagnoses with multiple components. RESULTS: The most likely diagnosis was most often correctly named by Claude Opus 4.6 (86.1%, 95% confidence interval [78.1; 91.6]), with GPT-5.4 close behind (85.1% [76.9; 90.8]). When partly correct answers were also counted, the three best-performing models all scored in the narrow range of 91.1-92.1%. The answers were highly stable. For diagnoses with multiple components, incorrect answers were more often incomplete than entirely wrong. CONCLUSION: LLMs have high diagnostic accuracy when challenged with published nephrological case scenarios. The interpretation of these findings is limited, however, because previous exposure of the models to individual vignettes, or parts thereof, cannot be ruled out. For clinical use, it must be borne in mind that plausible answers can be incomplete. Global accuracy measures may overestimate the diagnostic reliability of AI language models. The completeness and causal plausibility of the answers and their relevance to clinical action should be systematically investigated in benchmark studies.

title: Molecular Differentiation and Antibacterial Activity of in vitro-derived Paulownia Spp. Paulownia elongata, Paulownia tomentosa and Paulownia fortunei
abstractText: Paulownia is recognized as one of the most valuable and versatile tree species, gaining increasing attention for its industrial applications. Its growing demand is driven by its potential as a bioenergy source and raw wood industry material. Additionally, Paulownia species are being investigated for their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, making them promising candidates for therapeutic uses. Effective micropropagation protocols for Paulownia species have been developed, utilizing axillary buds and seeds to initiate in vitro culture. During the multiplication phase, a modified Murashige & Skoog (MS) medium was used to assess the effects of genotype and culture medium on seed germination and plantlet development across three different Paulownia genotypes: Paulownia elongata, Paulownia tomentosa, and Paulownia fortunei. Shoot tip explants were also employed for micropropagation, optimizing plant growth regulators. Molecular analyses were conducted to compare these species by amplifying genomic DNA with arbitrary primers via Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR). The DNA fragments were successfully amplified, and two PCR-based techniques, Random Amplified Polymorphic DNA (RAPD) and Inter-Simple Sequence Repeat (ISSR), were utilized to assess clonal stability and genetic variation. These markers, targeting distinct genomic regions, provided a thorough understanding of the genetic differences among the species. Protein levels were also analyzed across different Paulownia species, Total phenolic contents were recorded of the examined paulownia spp. and the antibacterial activity was tested against three strains of bacteria Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus cereus and E. Coli , showing promising antibacterial activity against two of the pathogenic strains Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus cereus providing valuable insights into developing a reliable micropropagation system to produce genetically identical and stable plants and on the other hand possess medical properties as antibacterial natural extracts. These findings enhance our understanding of how to improve Paulownia’s adaptability under diverse environmental conditions and optimize its production for commercial purposes.

title: Work stress and drug use behaviors for stress relief of medical representatives in Bangkok Metropolitan
abstractText: "Background: In 2021, the Department of Mental Health Thailand, found that 9.4% of Thais experience stress, with the highest rates in Bangkok at 14.1%, primarily attributed to work-related stress. One of the top 10 professions with the highest stress levels is medical representatives. Objectives: To study work-related stress and medication usage behaviors among pharmaceutical representatives in Bangkok and its suburbs, including factors influencing these behaviors and the correlation between stress levels and medication usage behaviors. Methods: Online data were collected from medical representatives responsible for Bangkok and its suburbs, aged ≥ 22 years, totaling 330 individuals. The study utilizes a questionnaire covering 1) personal information, 2) assessment of stress perceptions related to work factors, and 3) evaluation of stress-relieving medication usage behaviors. Results: The majority of participants were female with an average age of 33 years. Among pharmaceutical representatives, two-thirds reported moderate stress levels, averaging 50.6%. Regarding behaviors related to stress-relief medication, a significant majority, 62.8%, exhibited good practice. This study showed a significant positive correlation between drug use behaviors and stress levels among participants (P < 0.001). Conclusion: Medical representatives in Bangkok and its metropolitan area exhibit an average stress level score of 50.6 out of 100, with two-thirds reporting moderate to high stress levels related to work factors. Additionally, two-thirds of them demonstrate favorable behaviors towards using stress-relief medication. Specifically, 62.8% engage in these behaviors at a good level."

title: Prevalence of academic burnout and its association with the big five personality traits and social support among preclinical medical students at a University, Faculty of Medicine in Thailand
abstractText: "Background: Academic burnout is a mental health problem that adversely affects learning and quality of life among medical students, particularly during the preclinical years when students face intensive coursework, high academic demands, and persistent stress. Although academic burnout has been extensively investigated, evidence regarding the roles of the Big Five personality traits and social support among Thai medical students remains limited. Objective: To determine the prevalence of academic burnout and to identify the factors associated with and predictive of academic burnout among preclinical medical students at a faculty of medicine in Bangkok, Thailand. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 340 preclinical medical students during May–June 2024. Data were collected using self-administered questionnaires, including a personal information questionnaire, the Thai version of the Big Five Personality Inventory, a social support questionnaire, and the Maslach Burnout In ventory–Student Survey (MBI-SS). Associations between potential factors and academic burnout were examined using the Chi-square test and Fisher’s exact test. Predictive factors were identified using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Results: Among the 340 participants, 56.8% exhibited a high level of academic burnout in at least one burnout dimension. High burnout in one, two, and three dimensions was observed in 32.6%, 17.1%, and 7.1% of participants, respectively. Using the predefined criterion of high scores in all three dimensions—emotional exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced academic efficacy—the prevalence of academic burnout was 7.1%. Factors significantly associated with academic burnout included age > 21 years, being in the second or third year of study, psychiatric disorders, neutral to low satisfaction with medical education, infrequent or no regular exercise, preference for listening to music, sleep problems, sleeping pill use, low extraversion, low openness to experience, low conscientiousness, low emotional social support, and low overall social support. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified infrequent or no regular exercise and low openness to experience as significant predictors of academic burnout (P < 0.05), whereas neutral to low satisfaction with medical education, low extraversion, low conscientiousness, and low emotional social support showed stronger associations with academic burnout (P < 0.01). Conclusion: Academic burnout was common among preclinical medical students. Behavioral factors, personality traits, and social support were important contributors to burnout. These findings highlight the importance of promoting regular physical activity, strengthening emotional support, and developing personality-tailored interventions to prevent academic burnout and enhance psychological well-being among medical students."

title: Fetal bovine serum in cell culture
abstractText: "The purpose of this literature review is to summarize the procedures for producing fetal bovine serum (FBS), various testing standards, manufacturing sources, benefits, and applications of FBS in cell culture media preparation. FBS is the most widely used serum for in vitro eukaryotic cell culture. It is commonly used in biomedical research, drug development, and biomanufacturing. Due to its very low antibody levels and a higher content of growth factors, it is versatile in a wide range of cell culture applications. FBS is derived from peripheral blood collected from bovine fetuses through closed collection systems at slaughterhouses. A protein called bovine serum albumin (BSA) is the major component of FBS and plays a key role in maintaining osmotic balance and molecular transport within the cell culture medium. In addition to BSA, FBS is a rich source of growth and adhesion factors, lipids, hormones, nutrients, and electrolytes essential for supporting cell growth in culture. FBS is typically added to basic cell culture media such as Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) or Roswell Park Memorial Institute medium (RPMI) at concentrations of 5.0% – 20.0%."

title: "Determination of central-to-peripheral blood diazepam concentration ratio (C/P ratio) in Thai postmortem cases : a postmortem redistribution study"
abstractText: "Background: Interpretation of postmortem blood diazepam concentrations is important in establishing the cause of death. However, this may be complicated by postmortem redistribution (PMR). Currently, there is limited information regarding PMR of diazepam in the Thai people. Objective: To compare cardiac and femoral blood diazepam concentrations to examine PMR in Thai postmortem cases. Methods: A prospective study was performed on medico-legal cases sent for autopsy at the Department of Forensic Medicine, Siriraj Hospital. Thai individuals who were 18 years of age or older and had received diazepam during hospitalization were recruited. Cardiac and femoral blood samples were obtained during autopsy. Blood diazepam concentrations were analyzed, and the cardiac-to-femoral blood ratio (C/P ratio) was calculated. Statistical analysis was performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and the Mann–Whitney U test. Results: Forty two subjects were recruited for this study. The median/mean diazepam concentrations in cardiac and femoral blood were 52.0/83.1 ng/mL and 53.6/69.9 ng/mL, respectively. The median/mean C/P ratio of diazepam was 1.0/1.2. Diazepam concentrations in cardiac blood were not significantly different from those in femoral blood (P = 0.385). Although no significant correlation between the C/P ratio and body mass index, postmortem interval, or hospitalization time was observed, the C/P ratio was significantly higher in cases with chest injury than in cases without chest injury (P = 0.007). Conclusion: The median/mean C/P ratio of diazepam in Thai postmortem cases was 1.0/1.2. Chest injury was the only factor that had an impact on the C/P ratio of diazepam."

title: Early physical rehabilitation in critically ill patients : The role and application in intensive care units
abstractText: "Critically ill patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) often develop ICU-acquired weakness (ICU-AW). Early Mobilization (EM) is a vital intervention that initiates physical activity as early as possible after admission, from passive exercises to walking. This review article focuses on the scientific evidence supporting the use of early physical therapy rehabilitation in critically ill patients. It delves into the potential benefits of EM, exploring its role, application in the ICU, patient assessment, physical therapy guidelines, and the necessary tools and equipment. This review synthesizes findings from various research methodologies, including randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and meta-analyses published in recent years, to highlight the safety and efficacy of EM interventions in the ICU setting. The article also emphasizes the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and addresses the limitations and challenges of implementing EM. Scientific evidence suggests that starting physical therapy early in critically ill patients is safe and leads to positive outcomes. It helps prevent ICU-AW and reduces the risks associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation. In conclusion, promoting early physical therapy is crucial for improving the physical and mental well-being of critically ill patients. We emphasize the importance of tailoring EM programs to each patient’s unique condition to maximize the benefits of this lifechanging intervention."

title: "Comparison of short-term postoperative complications between free flap and locoregional flap reconstruction in stage III–IV oral cavity cancer"
abstractText: "Background: Optimal reconstruction for advanced oral cavity cancer requires balancing functional restoration against surgical morbidity. Free tissue transfer is the standard, yet locoregional flaps remain crucial in resource-limited settings. Their comparative short-term complication rates remain contested. Objective: To compare short-term postoperative complications between free flap and locoregional flap reconstruction in stage III–IV oral cavity cancer. Methods: A retrospective cohort study included 92 patients with stage III–IV oral squamous cell carcinoma who underwent immediate reconstruction at Buriram Hospital between August 2012 and August 2025. Patients were grouped into freeflap (n = 40) and locoregionalflap (n = 52) groups. The primary outcome was the 30-day overall complication rate. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of postoperative complications. Results: Overall complication rates were similar between free flap and locoregional flap groups (47.5% vs. 44.2%; P = 0.755). Operative time was longer for free flaps (P < 0.001), but hospital stay and mortality were comparable. Positive surgical margins were more common with locoregional flaps (46.2% vs. 15.0%; P = 0.002). Advanced disease stage was associated with increased complication risk; T4 stage was an independent predictor of postoperative complications, while nodepositive disease showed a similar trend. Conclusion: Free flap and locoregional flap reconstruction demonstrated comparable short-term complication rates in advanced oral cavity cancer. Complication risk appeared to be more strongly associated with advanced tumor burden than reconstruction technique. Flap selection should be individualized based on defect characteristics, patient factors, and available resources."

title: "Incidental CAC on non-gated chest CT : prognostic value for cardiovascular events in patients without prior cardiovascular disease"
abstractText: "Background: Non-gated chest computed tomography (CT) is routinely performed for the evaluation of thoracic conditions. Although the heart is not the primary focus of this examination, coronary artery calcification (CAC) is frequently encountered as an incidental finding and reflects underlying atherosclerotic burden. Objective: The study aimed to assess whether incidentally detected CAC on non-gated chest CT is associated with fiveyear cardiovascular outcomes in patients without prior cardiovascular disease (CVD). Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults aged 40-70 years who underwent non-gated chest CT at Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) General Hospital between July 2019 and June 2020. CAC was assessed using a visual coronary artery calcium (vCAC) scoring system. Demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, and cardiovascular events occurring within five years after the index CT were obtained from electronic medical records. Results: Incidental CAC (vCAC ≥1) was present in 54.3% of patients. Individuals with CAC were significantly older and had a higher burden of cardiometabolic risk factors. Cardiovascular events occurred more frequently in patients with CAC than in those without CAC (14.6% vs. 3.3%), corresponding to an approximately fourfold higher event rate. Event rates also increased with CAC severity (P < 0.001 for trend), with a notable increase observed among patients with vCAC scores ≥ 2. Conclusion: Incidental CAC on routine non-gated chest CT is associated with future cardiovascular events in patients without known CVD. Visual CAC assessment may provide clinically useful prognostic information and support opportunistic cardiovascular risk stratification in routine radiology practice."

title: Pediococcus acidilactici causing pyogenic hepatic abscess: A rare case report
abstractText: BACKGROUND Hepatic abscess refers to a focal collection of purulent material within the liver parenchyma, typically secondary to bacterial, fungal, or parasitic infections. Most hepatic abscesses (HA) are caused by Escherichia coli , Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Streptococci, or are polymicrobial. Pediococcus acidilactici (P. acidilactici ) is a Gram-positive coccus, rarely implicated in human infections. We report a case of P. acidilactici HA in a middle-aged male with no apparent risk factors, successfully treated with percutaneous drainage and beta-lactam antibiotics. CASE SUMMARY A 52 year old male presented with fever and abdominal pain. Initial labs revealed mild anemia, leukocytosis, and elevated alkaline phosphatase. Cross-sectional imaging demonstrated a multiloculated left HA, managed with computed tomography guided drainage. Culture of the abscess aspirate grew P. acidilactici, identified by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. The patient received beta-lactam antibiotics. Follow-up imaging showed that the HA had resolved two months after drainage and antibiotic treatment. CONCLUSION P. acidilactici should be considered a rare cause of pyogenic HA, even in immunocompetent patients without apparent predisposing factors. Prompt percutaneous drainage and targeted beta-lactam therapy were associated with a favorable outcome in this patient.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound in the acute abdomen and gastrointestinal emergencies: An evidence-based guide and the case for standardisation
abstractText: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is embedded in emergency assessment of acute abdominal pain, yet its evidence is scattered across emergency, surgical, anaesthetic and radiology journals. This structured narrative review synthesises four applications: (1) Small-bowel obstruction; (2) Gastric aspiration-risk assessment; (3) Non-traumatic free intraperitoneal fluid; and (4) Biliary disease including cholangitis. Sources came from a purposive search of PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science through August 2026, favouring the highest available evidence per application; it was English-language only, unregistered, and without review-level risk-of-bias appraisal or de novo pooling. We report thresholds, pooled sensitivities and specificities, likelihood ratios and, where retrievable, heterogeneity and risk-of-bias data. POCUS for small-bowel obstruction and cholecystitis is primarily a rule-in tool: A negative scan does not reliably exclude disease, and neither defines aetiology, ischaemia or perforation, for which computed tomography remains necessary. For non-traumatic free fluid the strongest rule-in evidence concerns suspected ectopic pregnancy; gastric POCUS stratifies aspiration risk against surrogate endpoints. We contribute an integrated, symptom-based, pretest-probability-driven algorithm with a competency precondition, a non-diagnostic exit and a defined action for every result; it is not prospectively validated. Dispersion across operators, thresholds and reference standards exceeds the margins bedside decisions turn on; we argue standardisation, not further accuracy estimation, is rate-limiting.

title: Safety and efficacy of 125 I radioactive seed strand implantation combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt for portal hypertension accompanied by portal vein tumor thrombus
abstractText: BACKGROUND In patients with cirrhotic portal hypertension complicated by portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) secondary to hepatocellular carcinoma, satisfactory therapeutic efficacy and long-term prognosis remain difficult to achieve with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) alone. A combined strategy incorporating portal vein implantation of radioactive 125I seed strands represents a therapeutic paradigm warranting thorough investigation. AIM To evaluate the safety and efficacy of 125I radioactive seed strand implantation combined with TIPS in patients with portal hypertension and PVTT. METHODS Clinical data from 187 consecutive patients with portal hypertension and PVTT treated at our institution between January 2019 and December 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Ultimately, 116 eligible patients were enrolled and divided into the TIPS-alone group (n = 56) and the TIPS combined with 125I seed strand implantation group (n = 60). Perioperative technical parameters, symptom relief rates, stent restenosis time, and survival outcomes were compared between the two groups. Patients were followed until death or loss to follow-up (median follow-up: 22.6 months, range: 1.2-65.7 months). Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression was employed to identify independent prognostic factors. RESULTS The technical success rate was 100%. The postoperative portal pressure gradient was significantly reduced compared with baseline (P < 0.001). The median overall survival was 13.93 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 10.03-15.97] in the combined group, which was significantly longer than the 8.99 months (95%CI: 6.45-11.53) observed in the TIPS-alone group (P = 0.0034). The cumulative survival rates at 6, 12, and 24 months were 88.33%, 53.33%, and 26.67% in the combined group, compared with 69.64%, 28.57%, and 12.5% in the control group, respectively. The symptom relief rate was markedly higher, and the stent restenosis rate was significantly lower in the combined group (hazard ratio = 0.227, 95%CI: 0.129-0.401, P < 0.001). Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified 125I seed strand implantation, Child-Pugh class, and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score as independent prognostic factors (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSION The combination of 125I radioactive seed strand implantation and TIPS is a safe and effective therapeutic strategy for patients with portal hypertension and PVTT, prolonging survival and reducing stent restenosis.

title: Non-cancer mortality in hepatocellular carcinoma: Population-based competing-risk study
abstractText: BACKGROUND Deaths unrelated to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) may be clinically relevant when patients survive long enough for age, chronic liver disease, cardiovascular disease, infection, and other conditions to influence mortality. Standard survival analyses may misrepresent this risk as HCC death precludes subsequent non-HCC death. AIM To estimate the cumulative incidence of non-HCC death and identify how its adjusted associations change during follow-up in a population-based HCC cohort. METHODS We analyzed 31274 adults with first primary HCC diagnosed during 2010-2015 in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results 17-registry database. Non-HCC death was the event of interest and HCC death was the competing event. Cumulative incidence functions were compared using Gray’s test. The primary regression used 19748 complete cases with known stage, tumor size, and alpha-fetoprotein status. Proportional subdistribution hazards were assessed with covariate-by-log(1 + time) terms. As the global assumption was violated, adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios were reported at 12 months, 36 months, and 60 months. A full-cohort missing-category Fine-Gray model and a cause-specific Cox model were sensitivity analyses. RESULTS During a reverse Kaplan-Meier median follow-up of 97 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 96-99], 22290 patients died from HCC and 3880 died from non-HCC causes; non-HCC deaths comprised 14.8% of all deaths. The cumulative incidence of non-HCC death was 6.2% (95%CI: 6.0%-6.5%) at 12 months, 9.8% (95%CI: 9.4%-10.1%) at 36 months, and 11.2% (95%CI: 10.8%-11.5%) at 60 months. The proportional subdistribution hazards assumption was rejected (global Wald χ 2 = 836.6, 21 df , P < 0.001). For age 75 years or older vs 18-49 years, adjusted subdistribution hazard ratios increased from 1.33 (95%CI: 1.15-1.53) at 12 months to 1.74 (95%CI: 1.40-2.17) at 60 months. Advanced stage and larger tumors showed lower subdistribution hazards but not consistently lower cause-specific hazards, a pattern compatible with dominant competing HCC mortality. Associations with recorded surgery and chemotherapy crossed the null over time and cannot be interpreted as treatment effects. CONCLUSION Non-HCC death accounted for approximately one in seven deaths after HCC diagnosis. Its associations were time dependent, and a single constant subdistribution hazard ratio obscured clinically important changes during follow-up. The findings support competing-risk assessment and continued management of non-cancer health risks, while treatment comparisons remain vulnerable to selection and survivor bias.

title: Acute kidney injury after liver cancer ablation: Risk factors and perioperative management
abstractText: BACKGROUND Evidence regarding the risk factors for and clinical management of acute kidney injury (AKI) following liver cancer (LC) ablation remains limited. AIM To investigate the incidence and potential risk factors for AKI following LC ablation and explore relevant clinical preventive strategies. METHODS This retrospective study included 168 patients with LC who underwent ablation between May 2022 and February 2026. Patients were classified into AKI (n = 25) and non-AKI (n = 143) groups according to postoperative AKI occurrence. Baseline characteristics, tumor-related characteristics (laterality, TNM stage, tumor size, tumor number, and ablation type), and laboratory parameters were compared between groups. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with AKI after LC ablation. RESULTS Age, diabetes, TNM stage, tumor size, hemoglobin (Hb), uric acid (UA), and serum creatinine (SCr) differed significantly between groups. Univariate analysis identified older age, diabetes, larger tumor size, higher UA, and higher SCr levels as potential risk factors, while higher Hb was associated with a lower risk of AKI. Multivariate analysis identified Hb and SCr as independent factors associated with AKI, with higher Hb associated with a lower risk [odds ratio (OR): 0.908, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.867-0.950, P < 0.001] and higher SCr associated with an increased risk (OR: 1.040, 95%CI: 1.004-1.078, P = 0.031). CONCLUSION Lower preoperative Hb and higher preoperative SCr levels may increase the risk of AKI after LC ablation. Preoperative anemia management and renal function assessment may help identify high-risk patients and guide individualized perioperative renal protection strategies.

title: Molecular pathophysiology of hepatocellular carcinoma: Role of tumor microenvironment and vascular signaling
abstractText: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for approximately 75%-85% of primary liver cancers and remains a top three cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with an estimated 900000 new cases and 830000 deaths annually. Despite advances demonstrated in recent phase III trials, median overall survival (OS) among patients with unresectable HCC treated with first-line immunotherapy and antiangiogenic combinations remains approximately 15-20 months, underscoring the biological aggressiveness of the disease. The molecular pathophysiology of HCC is shaped not only by recurrent genomic alterations including TP53 , TERT promoter, CTNNB1 , and chromatin-modifying genes but also by a chronically inflamed, fibrotic tumor microenvironment (TME) in which nuclear factor kappa-B, Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription, and transforming growth factor (TGF)-β signaling intersect with profound vascular remodeling. Aberrant angiogenesis represents a central hallmark of HCC. Immunohistochemical analyses demonstrate vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) positivity in approximately 65%-70% of tumors, with VEGF-expressing HCCs exhibiting significantly higher rates of capsular infiltration, microvascular invasion, intrahepatic metastasis, and inferior OS, with reported hazard ratios for death of approximately 1.5-2.0. In parallel, accumulation of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α and HIF-2α in hypoxic tumors and following locoregional therapies (e.g. , transarterial chemoembolization and radiofrequency ablation) transcriptionally activates VEGFA , ANGPT2 , CXCL12 , and glycolytic programs, driving neo-angiogenesis, vascular tortuosity, and metabolic reprogramming. Concurrent upregulation of MET , AXL , and fibroblast growth factor receptor signaling within tumor and stromal compartments further promotes invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and resistance to VEGF-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Non-parenchymal cells often constituting ≥ 50% of the tumor mass including liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, activated hepatic stellate cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and tumor-associated macrophages, secrete VEGF, ANGPT2 , interleukin-6, CCL2 , CXCL8 , and TGF-β, reinforcing vascular abnormalization and T-cell exclusion. These molecular circuits are directly leveraged in contemporary clinical trials. In IMbrave150, atezolizumab plus bevacizumab achieved a median OS of 19.2 months vs 13.4 months with sorafenib (hazard ratio 0.66), with 12-month OS rates of approximately 67% vs 55% and objective response rates of 27% vs 12% by RECIST 1.1. In HIMALAYA, the STRIDE regimen (tremelimumab plus durvalumab) produced a median OS of 16.4 months compared with 13.8 months for sorafenib (hazard ratio 0.78), with 36-month OS rates near 30% vs 20%, respectively. Exploratory analyses from these and related studies indicate that angiogenic, hypoxia-related, interferon-γ, and WNT/β-catenin gene signatures stratify clinical benefit and illuminate mechanisms of primary resistance to immune–antiangiogenic therapy. This review integrates molecular, TME-level, and clinical trial data to define biomarker-aligned, mechanism-based vascular and immune targeting strategies aimed at achieving more durable disease control in advanced HCC.

title: Preoperative prehabilitation within enhanced recovery after surgery for postoperative frailty and functional recovery following laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection
abstractText: BACKGROUND The incidence of postoperative frailty is elevated among patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery. However, enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS)-based preoperative interventions are frequently limited to health education and dietary advice, and adherence to prehabilitation protocols is poor, creating a need for structured and quantifiable perioperative intervention strategies. AIM To evaluate the effect of an ERAS-based preoperative prehabilitation management model, delivered through a mobile application, on postoperative frailty and functional recovery in patients undergoing laparoscopic colorectal cancer resection. METHODS This was a single-center, two-arm, parallel-group, assessor-blinded, superiority randomized controlled trial with a 1:1 allocation ratio. A total of 182 patients with colorectal cancer admitted to our hospital between October 2023 and October 2025 were enrolled and randomly assigned to a control group and an experimental group (n = 91 each) using a random number table. The control group received conventional ERAS perioperative management, whereas the experimental group received an ERAS-based preoperative prehabilitation management model combining structured exercise training, nutritional support, psychological intervention, and remote monitoring via a mobile application from admission until the day before surgery (≥ 14 days). The prespecified primary outcome was the incidence of postoperative frailty at 6 months after surgery. Secondary outcomes included Fried frailty scores, gastrointestinal recovery, mobility, inflammatory markers, quality of life, and postoperative complications. RESULTS All 182 randomized patients completed the study and were analyzed. At 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months postoperatively, Fried scores were lower in the experimental group than in the control group (P < 0.05). The incidence of frailty at 6 months postoperatively was 9.89% (9/91) in the experimental group vs 20.88% (19/91) in the control group [relative risk (RR): 0.47, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.23-0.99; risk difference (RD): -11.0%, 95%CI: -21.4% to -0.6%]. In the experimental group, the time to return of bowel sounds [mean difference (MD): -4.49 hours, 95%CI: -6.30 to -2.68], time to first flatus (MD: -3.66 hours, 95%CI: -6.23 to -1.09), time to first bowel movement (MD: -3.51 hours, 95%CI: -5.93 to -1.09), time to first oral intake (MD: -4.07 hours, 95%CI: -6.91 to -1.22), and postoperative length of hospital stay (MD: -1.50 days, 95%CI: -2.13 to -0.87) were all shorter than in the control group (P < 0.05). At 1 month and 6 months postoperatively, the experimental group's 6-minute walk test and Berg Balance Scale scores were higher than those of the control group (P < 0.05). At 7 days postoperatively, serum interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interferon-γ levels were lower in the experimental group than in the control group (P < 0.05). At 6 months postoperatively, scores for all dimensions of the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Colorectal were higher in the experimental group (P < 0.05). The incidence of postoperative complications was 2.20% (2/91) in the experimental group vs 9.89% (9/91) in the control group (RR: 0.22, 95%CI: 0.05-1.00; Fisher's exact P = 0.058; χ 2 test P = 0.029). CONCLUSION In this single-center randomized trial, an ERAS-based preoperative prehabilitation management model was associated with less postoperative frailty, faster gastrointestinal and motor recovery, attenuated inflammatory responses, and better quality of life after laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery. These findings require confirmation in prospectively registered, multicenter trials with longer follow-up before broader implementation can be recommended.

title: Trans-cinnamaldehyde alleviates hepatic steatosis and pyroptosis via SIRT1 activation in acute alcoholic liver injury
abstractText: BACKGROUND Acute alcoholic liver injury (ALI) is a hepatic disorder caused by excessive alcohol intake. The typical pathological features of ALI include hepatic lipid droplet accumulation, hepatocyte death, and inflammatory cell infiltration. Trans-cinnamaldehyde (TCA) is a natural aldehydic organic compound that exerts antibacterial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and lipid metabolism-regulating effects. However, whether TCA can alleviate acute ALI remains unclear. AIM To investigate the therapeutic targets of TCA for the treatment of acute ALI through transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation. METHODS We established a mouse model of acute ALI in vivo by oral gavage administration of ethanol (5 g/kg, 50% v/v) to investigate the protective effects of TCA against ethanol-induced hepatic steatosis and cell death. In vitro , we explored the mechanisms by which TCA regulates the sirtuin 1/peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (SIRT1/PPARα) pathway, fatty acid β-oxidation, and pyroptosis through SIRT1 gene silencing. RESULTS Our study found that TCA treatment (40 mg/kg) significantly reduced serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase activities, as well as hepatic total cholesterol and triglyceride levels in mice with acute ALI. Furthermore, TCA treatment markedly attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and hepatocyte death. Analysis of the Gene Expression Omnibus database (GSE28619) from patients with alcoholic hepatitis revealed significant enrichment of the adenosine 5’-monophosphate-activated protein kinase and PPAR signaling pathways. Mechanistically, TCA activated SIRT1/PPARα signaling. Notably, SIRT1 silencing abrogated the protective effects of TCA against acute ALI, including the amelioration of hepatic steatosis, enhancement of fatty acid β-oxidation, and suppression of ER stress-related proteins such as glucose-regulated protein 78, phosphorylated inositol-requiring enzyme 1α, C/EBP homologous protein and pyroptosis-associated proteins such as NOD -like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3, cleaved cysteinyl aspartate specific proteinase-1 (cleaved caspase-1), N-terminal gasdermin D. CONCLUSION TCA alleviated hepatocyte lipid deposition, ER stress and cell death in acute ALI by promoting SIRT1 activity, suggesting that TCA is a potential therapeutic agent for ALI.
