title: Exploring the role of apolipoproteins in hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure
abstractText: BACKGROUND Hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF) carries high mortality, yet current prognostic tools lack molecular precision. AIM To investigate the involvement of apolipoproteins (APO) in HBV-ACLF through using proteomics analyses. METHODS We analyzed serum samples from 10 healthy controls and 20 patients with HBV-ACLF treated with a plasma exchange-centered artificial liver support system (10 survivors, 10 non-survivors) using quanititative proteomics via data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. Differential protein expression (fold-change ≥ 1.2 or ≤ 0.833, P < 0.05) was analyzed using Gene Ontology and protein–protein interaction network tools. Clinical parameters like liver enzymes and bilirubin were assessed concurrently. RESULTS Among more than 200 differentially expressed proteins, he levels of APOL1, APOA1, APOC1, APOC2, and APOH were significantly lower in the HBV-ACLF groups than in the control groups, and the levels of APOC1, APOC2, and APOH were significantly lower in non-survivors than in survivor group. However, after adjusting for confounding factors, the differences were not statistically significant. Furthermore, the combined diagnosis panel of APOL1 and APOA1 showed the highest diagnostic accuracy for HBV-ACLF, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.940 (P = 0.0001). Similarly, the combination of APOC2 and APOH yielded the highest predictive performance for non-survival, achieving an AUC of 0.990 (P = 0.0002). The protein-protein interaction network positioned APO as hubs in lipid metabolism and inflammation pathways. CONCLUSION These APO may provide new clues for early detection and prognostic risk stratification of HBV-ACLF. Large sample studies are needed to validate our findings in the future.

title: The nearby Type II supernova 2024ggi beyond 600 days: Circumstellar interaction and dust formation
abstractText: The Type II supernova (SN) 2024ggi is one of the nearest core-collapse supernovae (SNe) to have exploded in recent decades. Its proximity has enabled extensive multiwavelength monitoring from early times through the nebular phase. Signatures of late-time interaction between the SN ejecta and hydrogen-rich circumstellar material (CSM) have recently been reported. Here we extend its study using late-time optical photometry and spectroscopy from 570 to 820 d after explosion. We investigate the emergence and evolution of late-time ejecta--CSM interaction and constrain the geometry of the interaction region and the properties of newly formed dust. We present optical light curves and a series of low-resolution optical spectra of SN 2024ggi covering phases between 570 and 820 d after explosion. Comparisons with other interacting SNe II and with synthetic spectra are presented. We model the Hα profile with the Monte Carlo radiative-transfer code , including both gas and dust components. Damocles Spectroscopic signatures of interaction precede photometric flattening. The spectra evolve from ejecta-dominated to interaction-dominated as Hα develops a broad, boxy profile. The optical light curves subsequently flatten relative to the 56 Co decay rate at approximately 650--670 d. The emission lines show a systematic blue-to-red asymmetry that requires a newly formed dust component within the ejecta. The inferred dust mass formed in the ejecta is 10^ -6 -10^ -5 M_⊙ if the grains are amorphous carbon or a carbon--silicate mixture, but can reach up to 10^ -3 M_⊙ for pure silicates. By ≳ 600 d, the optical evolution of SN 2024ggi is dominated by ejecta--CSM interaction, while the asymmetric line profiles provide evidence of recent dust formation. Our observations and findings regarding SN 2024ggi add to the growing number of SNe II observed several hundred days after explosion, demonstrating the diversity in late-time interaction and constraining the mass-loss histories of these massive star explosions.

title: Expression and role of the long noncoding RNA Linc00909 in chemoradiotherapy for colorectal cancer
abstractText: BACKGROUND Colorectal cancer is one of the major malignant tumors worldwide. Previous studies have shown that long noncoding RNAs have significant effects on various human cancers, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. AIM To investigate the impact of the long noncoding RNA Linc00909 on colorectal cancer and its molecular mechanism. METHODS Using 196 paired colorectal cancer and adjacent tissues from 30 patients with rectal cancer (19 resistant, 11 sensitive) to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, we assessed Linc00909 expression using real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction and correlated it with survival outcomes. Functional assays in Linc00909-overexpressing SW620 and DLD1 cells—including Cell Counting Kit-8 assays, flow cytometry, and sphere formation—evaluated proliferation, cell cycle, apoptosis, stemness, and 5-fluorouracil/radiotherapy sensitivity. Tumorigenicity was examined in vivo . Bioinformatic and molecular experiments explored Linc00909’s competing endogenous RNA mechanism. RESULTS Linc00909 was upregulated in resistant and tumor tissues and independently predicted poorer overall and disease-free survival. Linc00909 overexpression enhanced proliferation, colony formation, antiapoptotic capacity, stemness, and therapy resistance in vitro and promoted tumor growth in vivo . miR-625-5p was bioinformatically predicted and experimentally validated as a binding target of Linc00909, with its expression decreasing upon Linc00909 overexpression. SOX2 was identified as a downstream target of miR-625-5p and showed increased expression at both the messenger RNA and protein levels following Linc00909 upregulation. CONCLUSION Linc00909 can affect the proliferation, colony formation, apoptosis, cell cycle regulation, spheroid-forming ability, and sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to 5-fluorouracil and radiotherapy. Mechanistically, Linc00909 may regulate the expression of the downstream target gene SOX2 by sequestering miR-625-5p, thereby influencing the sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Therefore, Linc00909 can be considered a potential therapeutic target for treating colorectal cancer.

title: Liver transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma: Mechanisms, risk stratification, and evolving treatment landscape
abstractText: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), remains a leading cause of mortality. This article addresses the mechanisms underlying post-transplant HCC recurrence and evaluates current evidence-based strategies for diagnosis and management. Based on a targeted narrative review of high-impact literature published between 2010 and 2025, we synthesize evidence on the interplay between immunosuppression, tumor biology, and host-related factors driving recurrence. Using HCC recurrence after liver transplantation as the principal model, we critically examine existing risk stratification systems and surveillance protocols. We further summarize multimodal therapeutic approaches, ranging from curative-intent local therapies for oligo-recurrence to systemic treatments for advanced stages, where prognosis remains poor. Additionally, we discuss the emerging and controversial role of adjuvant therapies in high-risk populations. The review highlights areas of consensus, ongoing controversies, and key gaps in knowledge that require further investigation to improve long-term post-transplant outcomes. Particular attention is given to the role of immunosuppressive regimen modulation and emerging biomarker-driven surveillance strategies aimed at earlier detection and individualized risk prediction in post-transplant patients to ultimately improve survival and clinical decision-making.

title: Hepatocyte identity across steatosis-resolving therapies: Integrative transcriptomic and functional assessment
abstractText: BACKGROUND Approximately 30% of adults worldwide have metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. The extent to which therapies that resolve steatosis preserve hepatocyte transcriptional identity beyond reducing lipid accumulation remains unclear. AIM To re-analyze bulk RNA-sequencing data from APOB -mutant human liver organoids treated for seven days with acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibition, diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2 inhibition, fatty acid synthase inhibition, farnesoid X receptor agonism, or fibroblast growth factor 19 (GSE221705; 12 samples from two donors). METHODS Analyses included DESeq2 differential expression analysis; three functional scores for steatosis modulation, hepatocyte identity, and stress-pathway responses; a weighted Therapeutic Trade-off Score; gene-level bootstrap confidence intervals; and exploratory single-cell contextualization of 3293 human hepatocytes from GSE136103. RESULTS Diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2 inhibition ranked first in the exploratory framework, with the highest steatosis modulation score (-0.032), highest hepatocyte identity score (0.726), and a near-neutral mean stress score (-0.001). The lack of significantly differentially expressed genes for diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2 inhibition likely reflects limited statistical power, small transcriptomic effects, or no detectable effects under the conditions studied. CONCLUSION These preliminary findings support diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2 inhibition as a potential metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease strategy, but need to be validated in larger, clinically annotated cohorts given the limited sample size, post hoc signature selection, and single-cell pseudoreplication. This is deferred for future work.

title: Imaging-independent model for predicting choledocholithiasis in acute biliary pancreatitis
abstractText: BACKGROUND Predicting choledocholithiasis (CDL) in acute biliary pancreatitis remains challenging, and unnecessary endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatographies (ERCPs) should be avoided due to their risks. Current stratification tools for indicating ERCP include imaging findings, potentially leading to diagnostic variability across imaging modalities and between observers. AIM To stratify patients independent of imaging we developed a machine learning–based model using easily available parameters. METHODS In this observational study we retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of 601 patients coded with ICD-10 for biliary pancreatitis. After exclusions, we analyzed 348 patients with acute biliary pancreatitis at LMU University Hospital, between 2005 and 2021. Using 14 features-excluding common bile duct (CBD) width-a random forest model was trained and evaluated for sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUC-ROC) curve. RESULTS Among 348 patients, 167 (48.0%) had confirmed CBD stones. The model achieved a sensitivity of 92.3%, a negative predictive value (NPV) of 78.6%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.739. Compared to guideline-recommended predictors such as CBD width ≥ 8 mm (sensitivity 79.5%, NPV 68.0%) or bilirubin ≥ 4 mg/dL (sensitivity 30.8%, NPV 47.1%), our model showed superior performance and missed significantly fewer intraductal concrements [4.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.5%-11.9%] vs 11.4% (95%CI: 5.9%-21.0%) and 38.6% (95%CI: 28.1%-50.3%). CONCLUSION This model for predicting CDL in acute pancreatitis without relying on CBD width may be a valuable tool to reduce ERCPs, especially in centers without access to daily endoscopic ultrasound.

title: Hepatitis B surface antigen-targeting strategies for clearance: A review of progress from mechanistic exploration to clinical translation
abstractText: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) persistence hinders the achievement of a functional cure in patients with chronic hepatitis B. Strategies to suppress or eliminate HBsAg and break the host immune tolerance while restoring immune response become key components of immune therapy-directed clinical cure. Agents that target HBsAg include monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, gene editing technologies, capsid assembly modulators, and therapeutic agents targeting secretion pathways. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and other immune-based clearance approaches are also included within this strategic framework. These agents target the HBsAg lifecycle and its source templates, including covalently closed circular DNA and integrated hepatitis B virus DNA in the host genome. This article reviews these strategies by synthesizing the latest information from preclinical studies and clinical trials, summarises their mechanisms and efficacy, discusses challenges and prospects for combinations, and aims to provide a scientific basis for chronic hepatitis B curative research.

title: Self-reported open cholecystectomy training, practice, and confidence in the laparoscopic era: An international convenience-sample survey
abstractText: BACKGROUND Open cholecystectomy has become an infrequently performed rescue operation that is required precisely when laparoscopic dissection is unsafe, when the critical view of safety cannot be obtained, or when bile duct injury is suspected. The training that supports this operation in the laparoscopic era is poorly characterized at the surgeon level, and it is not known how often standardized assessment or simulation-based training for emergency conversion is actually delivered. AIM To describe self-reported operative exposure, structured training, intraoperative practice and confidence regarding open cholecystectomy among surgeons responding to an internationally disseminated survey. METHODS Anonymous cross-sectional online survey using an investigator-designed 24-item questionnaire disseminated by nonprobability convenience sampling through professional messaging groups of general, trauma and emergency, and hepatopancreatobiliary surgeons and through the channels of a national surgical society between July 2025 and February 2026; no sampling frame was defined and no response rate could be calculated. Eligible respondents were general surgery residents, fellows and attending surgeons. Analyses were descriptive and item-level; primary estimates are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CI), and no inferential comparisons were performed. Cumulative open cholecystectomy volume is additionally presented stratified by years of practice and by current role. The internal structure of the instrument was examined in a separate psychometric evaluation reported as Supplementary material . Confidence items were recorded on 5-point ordinal scales with explicit verbal anchors and are reported as complete response distributions. The instrument did not include an item on country or region of practice. RESULTS All 391 submitted questionnaires were complete and non-duplicate and were analyzed (270 attendings, 105 residents, 16 fellows); 68.3% (95%CI: 63.5-72.7) reported more than 100 laparoscopic cholecystectomies as primary surgeon, compared with 37.6% (95%CI: 32.9-42.5) for open cholecystectomy; 29.7% (95%CI: 25.4-34.4) reported 10 or fewer open cases. Direct observation by a supervisor was reported by 83.1% (95%CI: 79.1-86.5), but formal standardized assessment with the Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills or the Global Operative Assessment of Laparoscopic Skills was reported by only 20.7% (95%CI: 17.0-25.0), and simulation or hands-on training addressing emergency conversion by 16.4% (95%CI: 13.0-20.4). Intraoperative cholangiography was used selectively by 69.8% and indocyanine green fluorescence was never used by 77.5%. Self-reported confidence was concentrated in the highest category for the cystic pedicle (55.5%) and the critical view of safety (53.7%), but dispersed across all categories for common bile duct exploration and for identification and repair of bile duct injury, for which 32.5% (95%CI: 28.0-37.3) selected the two lowest categories. The instrument did not support a unidimensional measurement model, so all results are reported item by item. CONCLUSION Among these self-selected respondents, open cholecystectomy exposure, standardized assessment and conversion-specific simulation were heterogeneous and frequently limited, and self-reported confidence fell sharply for the biliary scenarios in which open expertise is most consequential. These findings concern self-reported confidence rather than objective competence and do not describe a defined surgical workforce.

title: Nanostructured propolis attenuates experimental liver fibrosis and is associated with changes in LC3 and p62 expression
abstractText: BACKGROUND Liver fibrosis is characterized by persistent activation of hepatic stellate cells and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, and effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. AIM To investigate whether nanostructuring enhances the antifibrotic efficacy of propolis against carbon tetrachloride (CCL4)-induced liver fibrosis and examined its association with changes in the autophagy-related markers microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) and sequestosome 1 (p62). METHODS Male Sprague-Dawley rats were exposed to CCL4 for eight weeks with or without concomitant administration of conventional propolis or propolis nanoparticles. Biochemical, histopathological, oxidative stress, and molecular analyses were performed, including assessment of LC3 and p62 expression at the mRNA and immunohistochemical protein levels. RESULTS CCL4 administration induced marked hepatic injury, oxidative stress, and liver fibrosis, accompanied by increased LC3 expression and reduced p62 expression. Both propolis formulations attenuated these alterations; however, propolis nanoparticles produced more pronounced improvements in biochemical, histopathological, oxidative stress, and molecular parameters than conventional propolis and were associated with partial attenuation of the CCL4-induced changes in LC3 and p62 expression. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that nanoformulation may improve the antifibrotic efficacy of propolis in experimental liver fibrosis. The observed alterations in LC3 and p62 were associated with the protective effects of propolis nanoparticles; however, because autophagic flux was not directly assessed, these findings should be interpreted as changes in autophagy-related marker expression rather than definitive evidence of altered autophagic activity. Further studies are warranted to clarify the underlying mechanisms and evaluate the translational potential of this approach.

title: Silencing of thrombospondin-1 prevents abdominal adhesion formation by reducing inflammation and oxidative stress
abstractText: BACKGROUND Intraperitoneal adhesions are fibrotic scars that form between abdominal organs after surgery and a major cause of postsurgical morbidity. Despite their clinical significance, the precise molecular mechanisms underlying their formation remain largely unclear, and standardized therapeutic strategies have yet to be established. AIM To investigate the role of thrombospondin-1 (Thbs-1) in peritoneal adhesion formation and evaluate its potential as a therapeutic target. METHODS A standardized peritoneal adhesion model was developed. Thbs-1 -knockdown mice and HMrSV5 cell lines were established. Twenty-five mice were randomized to five treatment groups: Sham, negative control, sh-Thbs-1, normal saline, and Leu-Ser-Lys-Leu (LSKL). Adhesion severity was assessed 7 days post-surgery by Nair’s score and through immunohistochemistry, multi-immunofluorescence, and oxidative stress assays. RESULTS Thbs-1 was found to be highly expressed during adhesion formation. Both sh-Thbs-1 and LSKL treatments significantly attenuated adhesion formation, resulting in lower Nair’s and inflammatory scores. Mechanistically, Thbs-1 deficiency reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation and promoted peritoneal mesothelial cell repair, as evidenced by CK19 labeling and Sirius red staining. In vitro , Thbs-1 knockdown protected HMrSV5 cells from rapid proliferation and oxidative stress damage. CONCLUSION Thbs-1 deficiency reduces adhesion formation by inhibiting inflammation and ROS production while promoting mesothelial repair. Accordingly, Thbs-1 represents a promising therapeutic target for postsurgical adhesions.

title: Drug-Related Problems and Potentially Inappropriate Medications among Elderly Patients with Diabetes Mellitus: A Prospective Observational Study
abstractText: Background: Older adults with diabetes mellitus frequently require multiple medications because of multimorbidity, increasing the complexity of pharmacotherapy and the risk of drug-related problems (DRPs) and potentially inappropriate medications (PIMs). Systematic identification of inappropriate prescribing is therefore important for improving medication safety in this vulnerable population. Objectives: To identify PIMs among elderly patients with diabetes mellitus using the 2019 American Geriatrics Society (AGS) Beers Criteria and to characterize the associated DRPs and their underlying causes using the Pharmaceutical Care Network Europe (PCNE) Classification V9.1. Methodology: A prospective observational study was conducted over 6 months in the General Medicine Department of HKES’s Basaveshwar Teaching and General Hospital, Kalaburagi. Patients aged >65 years with diabetes mellitus who were prescribed at least two medications and fulfilled the predefined eligibility criteria were enrolled. Demographic characteristics, diagnoses, comorbidities, medication profiles and relevant clinical information were recorded using a structured data collection form. PIMs were identified using the 2019 AGS Beers Criteria and the identified PIMs were subsequently classified according to the PCNE V9.1 framework. Results: A total of 120 elderly patients were evaluated. Most patients were aged 65–75 years (101; 84.17%) and were male (72; 60.0%). Diabetes with hypertension was the predominant comorbidity (73; 60.8%). Major polypharmacy (>5 medications) was present in 114 patients (95.0%), with a mean of 11 medications prescribed per patient. A total of 218 PIMs were identified. The largest Beers category was drug–disease/drug–syndrome interactions (56; 25.7%), followed by medications to be avoided (50; 22.9%), renal impairment-related criteria (42; 19.3%), medications to be used with caution (37; 17.0%) and clinically important drug–drug interactions (33; 15.1%). Glimepiride (18), nifedipine (12), insulin (9), paroxetine (22), canagliflozin (15), tramadol (9) and levetiracetam (19) were among the frequently identified agents across the respective Beers categories. Drug selection was the principal PCNE cause domain, accounting for 192 DRPs (88.9%). Conclusion: The study demonstrated a substantial burden of PIMs and medication-related safety concerns among elderly patients with diabetes mellitus, occurring in the setting of extensive polypharmacy and multimorbidity. Systematic medication review using explicit prescribing criteria, renal and dose assessment, and structured DRP classification may facilitate earlier identification of potentially harmful prescribing patterns. Integration of clinical pharmacists into multidisciplinary medication-review processes may further support individualized and safer pharmacotherapy.

title: Peripheral immune landscape in hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure: Tumor necrosis factor-α, M1-like macrophages, and lymphocyte exhaustion
abstractText: BACKGROUND Hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF) is a critical illness with high 28-day mortality. It is associated with immunometabolic-mediated systemic inflammation leading to multi-organ failure. AIM To investigate the peripheral immune landscape in patients with HBV-ACLF, with particular attention to the associations among tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) levels, M1 macrophage polarization, and lymphocyte exhaustion. METHODS In this prospective cross-sectional study of 97 subjects (healthy controls, chronic hepatitis B, and HBV-ACLF), flow cytometry and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay quantified peripheral immune profiles and cytokines. Independent associated factors were identified via least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and multivariable logistic regression. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to all intergroup comparisons and correlation analyses. RESULTS HBV-ACLF patients exhibited profound peripheral immune remodeling, featuring a pro-inflammatory shift toward M1-like monocyte/macrophage polarization accompanied by compensatory upregulation of M2-like monocytes/macrophages and a sharp escalation in serum TNF-α, interferon-gamma, and interleukin (IL)-6 ( all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation selected 9 feature variables, and after iterative variance inflation factor refinement, 6 variables were retained. Firth’s bias-reduced logistic regression identified elevated TNF-α as an independent associated factor [odds ratio (OR) = 1.359, 95%CI: 1.056-1.749, P = 0.017]. Notably, TNF-α and IL-6 exhibited strong collinearity (Spearman rho = 0.834); sensitivity analysis substituting IL-6 for TNF-α yielded consistent findings (IL-6: OR = 1.187, 95%CI: 1.052-1.339, P = 0.005). Stratified and correlation analyses revealed that high TNF-α and M1-like monocyte/macrophage polarization positively correlated with clinical severity (total bilirubin, creatinine) and negatively with lymphocyte percentages, while M2-like monocytes/macrophages positively correlated with neutrophil ratio (FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). Staging analysis showed a synchronized TNF-α surge, M1 shift, and deep lymphocyte depletion during mid-to-late stages (prothrombin activity ≤ 30%). CONCLUSION This study systematically characterized the coexistence of pro-inflammatory remodeling and immune exhaustion within the peripheral immune landscape of HBV-ACLF, identifying TNF-α as a key immunopathological associated factor. These findings highlight the potential value of targeting TNF-α and monitoring multi-lineage immune crosstalk for risk stratification and therapeutic intervention in HBV-ACLF.

title: Association between fibrosis-4 index and all-cause mortality by hepatic steatosis category in United States adults: A retrospective cohort study
abstractText: BACKGROUND The hepatic steatosis index (HSI) and fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) are readily calculated from routinely collected clinical data; they share aminotransferase components, while FIB-4 is also strongly influenced by age and platelet count. We hypothesized that the association between FIB-4 and mortality would vary across established HSI screening categories and that combining the indices would provide limited incremental prognostic information. AIM To evaluate associations between FIB-4 and mortality across HSI categories and assess the incremental predictive value of both indices. METHODS This retrospective cohort study included adults aged ≥ 45 years who participated in the 1999-2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, with mortality follow-up through 2019. HSI was categorized as < 30, 30-36, or > 36, and elevated FIB-4 was defined using age-specific thresholds. HSI and FIB-4 were surrogate indices, and the primary cohort lacked imaging or histologic confirmation of steatotic liver disease or fibrosis. Mortality associations were evaluated using survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and period-specific models. Incremental prediction was evaluated using Harrell’s C-index, time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, Brier score, and apparent calibration. Missing-data robustness was assessed using multiple imputation. RESULTS Among 27197 participants (6654 deaths), the fully adjusted complete-case model included 21695 participants (5079 deaths), excluding 5502 participants with missing covariate data. Fully adjusted hazard ratios for elevated vs low FIB-4 were 1.132 (95%CI: 0.931-1.376), 1.350 (1.223-1.491), and 1.173 (1.063-1.295) in the HSI < 30, 30-36, and > 36 groups, respectively. The overall interaction was not statistically significant (P = 0.098). Both indices showed nonlinear associations with mortality. Period-specific estimates were not statistically significant beyond 10 years of follow-up, and effect modification was not consistent over time. The pooled interaction remained statistically nonsignificant after multiple imputation (P = 0.056). Adding both indices to the base clinical model increased Harrell’s C-index by 0.00319 (95%CI: 0.00190-0.00447), whereas adding their interaction provided no further improvement. CONCLUSION Elevated FIB-4 was associated with mortality in HSI 30-36 and > 36, but not significantly in HSI < 30; the overall interaction was nonsignificant, and predictive improvement did not establish clinical utility.

title: Minimally invasive surgeries for hepatic echinococcosis in patients with situs inversus totalis: Two case reports
abstractText: BACKGROUND Situs inversus totalis (SIT), also known as “mirror-image anatomy”, is a rare congenital malformation with complete mirror reversal of all abdominal and thoracic viscera, which drastically increases the difficulty of surgery due to altered anatomical landmarks and operative orientation. Hepatic echinococcosis is a rare zoonotic parasitic liver disease, and complete pericystectomy remains the gold standard for radical treatment. The coexistence of SIT and hepatic echinococcosis creates dual surgical challenges, and that have never been reported globally. CASE SUMMARY We report two cases of minimally invasive surgeries for hepatic echinococcosis in patients with SIT: One was remote robotic-assisted hepatic hydatid cyst resection, and the other was pure laparoscopic complete pericystectomy of hepatic echinococcosis. The both procedures were successfully completed with favorable perioperative outcomes. Our report elaborate on the key technical difficulties, individualized operative strategies, and innovative clinical value of the minimally invasive approaches for SIT patients. CONCLUSION This report provides practical references for the diagnosis and surgical management of hepatic echinococcosis in patients with SIT.

title: Clinical features and associated factors for clinically significant portal hypertension in patients with histologically early-stage primary biliary cholangitis
abstractText: BACKGROUND Clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) is traditionally associated with advanced liver fibrosis, but its occurrence and predictors in histologically early stage primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) remain unclear. AIM To identify clinical features and independent risk factors for CSPH in patients with biopsy proven early stage (Scheuer stage I–II) PBC, facilitating early recognition and targeted intervention. METHODS This retrospective study enrolled 110 patients with histologically early-stage PBC at Beijing Ditan Hospital (2020-2023). Patients were divided into CSPH (n = 27) and non CSPH (n = 83) groups based on Baveno VII criteria. Demographic, laboratory, elastographic, and ultrasonographic data were compared. Multivariate logistic regression was used to determine independent predictors. RESULTS Both groups were predominantly middle-aged women. The CSPH group had significantly lower white blood cell count, hemoglobin, platelet, albumin, cholinesterase, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels, and higher total bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and total bile acid levels (all P < 0.05). Drug allergy history (29.6% vs 8.4%, P < 0.05) and histological stage II (63.0% vs 39.8%, P < 0.05) were more frequent in the CSPH group. Autoantibody profiles (anti-mitochondrial antibodies, antinuclear antibody, anti-centromere, anti-sp100, anti-gp210) and immunoglobulin levels did not differ between groups. Imaging showed larger portal vein diameter and higher liver stiffness in the CSPH group (both P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified drug allergies [odds ratio (OR) = 5.948, 95%CI: 1.494-23.675, P = 0.011] and main portal vein diameter (OR = 2.563, 95%CI: 1.635-4.017, P < 0.001) as independent factors associated with CSPH. CONCLUSION CSPH is not rare in histologically early-stage PBC, especially at stage II, and is accompanied by worse liver function and cytopenias. Drug allergy history and increased portal vein diameter are independently associated with CSPH, whereas common autoantibodies appear unrelated. These findings may help stratify early-stage PBC patients at risk of CSPH, though prospective validation is warranted.

title: Current awareness and influencing factors regarding digital out-of-hospital health monitoring among patients after gastrointestinal surgery: A cross-sectional study
abstractText: BACKGROUND Postoperative patients in gastrointestinal surgery often face interrupted professional care and insufficient rehabilitation guidance after discharge. Digital out-of-hospital health monitoring can provide remote monitoring and abnormality alerts, yet its effectiveness depends on patients' adequate cognition of the service. Currently, there is a lack of research on the cognitive status and influencing factors in this population. AIM To investigate the cognitive status of digital out-of-hospital health monitoring among postoperative patients in gastrointestinal surgery and analyze its influencing factors. METHODS A convenience sampling method was used to select 126 postoperative patients discharged from the gastrointestinal surgery department of a tertiary hospital. A self-designed cognitive questionnaire (4 dimensions, 15 items, Likert 5-point scale) was administered. A t test, analysis of variance, and multiple linear regression were used to analyze influencing factors. RESULTS The mean item score of cognition among the 126 patients was (3.02 ± 0.43), indicating a moderately low level. The value cognition dimension scored the highest, while the concern cognition dimension scored the lowest. Univariate analysis showed that age, education level, years of smartphone use, and health app use experience significantly affected the total cognitive score (all P < 0.05). Multiple regression analysis revealed that years of smartphone use (β = 0.203) and health app use experience (β = -0.176) were independent influencing factors. CONCLUSION Postoperative patients in gastrointestinal surgery exhibit generally low cognition of digital out-of-hospital health monitoring, characterized by a "value recognition preceding basic cognition" pattern and prevalent concerns. Digital contact experience predicts cognitive level better than demographic characteristics. Stratified health education should be implemented to strengthen service concept awareness, while technical optimization should be adopted to alleviate patient concerns.

However, the structure of their neutral atomic hydrogen ( (R)). title: Non-evolutionary effects on period change in Magellanic Cepheids. III. Empirical connection with additional low-amplitude variability
abstractText: The subject of the observed-minus-calculated ( method in classical Cepheids is generally associated with the measurement of secular period change, which is also known as evolutionary period change. While this offers a direct way to track the evolution of a star, the technique also helps uncover period variations on shorter timescales (non-evolutionary period changes). In our previous works, we compiled a large sample of Magellanic classical Cepheids that manifest irregularities in their diagrams, finding irregular period changes in ∼33% of the sample. The study, however, deliberately excluded Cepheids showing additional low-amplitude variability, which provides the context for the present work. We aim to establish whether the first-overtone Cepheids hosting additional low-amplitude variability differ from the general first-overtone population in terms of their period-change behaviour. Including this population brings the census of irregular period changes in Magellanic Cepheids a step closer to completeness. We analysed a sample of 544 Magellanic Cepheids with additional low-amplitude variability, using Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE) photometry. Specifically, these are Cepheids with a period ratio of (i) ∼ 0.60--0.65 or (ii) ∼ 0.68. This sample was investigated for period changes using diagrams, and the detected period changes were classified and characterised with several statistical methods following the methodology of our previous studies. We then combined these results with our previous first-overtone sample to update the incidence rates of the period-change classes. Based on their diagrams, we classified these Cepheids into three categories: class 1 (constant period), class 2 (linear period change), and class 3 (irregular period change). We find irregular period changes in 339 first-overtone Cepheids (195 in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) and 144 in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC)), corresponding to an incidence rate of ∼75.5%. This is only modestly higher than the ∼68.1% found for the far larger single-mode, first-overtone sample of our previous study. Including our candidates only shifts the combined first-overtone incidence marginally, to ∼69.7%. For the first time, we provide an empirical connection between additional low-amplitude variability and irregular period changes in first-overtone Cepheids. In our additional-variability sample, irregular period changes are more prominent, showing a statistically significant increase over purely single-mode Cepheids. At a fixed pulsation period, the irregularity strength anti-correlates with the dominant pulsation amplitude but not with the additional-signal amplitude, suggesting that the additional periodicity marks a weakly saturated pulsation state rather than driving the irregularity. We further detect cycle-to-cycle (C2C) period variation in 37% of the class 3 sample, with the associated C2C jitter strength (σ_η) roughly seven times larger than in non-Blazhko RRc stars and scaling with pulsation period at a shallower slope. In the future, extending the study of period changes to other Cepheid types, in particular Type-II Cepheids, will further probe the origin of these irregularities.

title: Sailing with the winds of HL Tau: The JWST view
abstractText: It is crucial to investigate protostellar ejections for understanding the formation of young stars and planetary systems. The Class I/II star HL Tau, with its well-studied ringed disk and prominent bipolar outflows, is a benchmark system for these studies. We provide a first overview of our Cycle 3 Space Telescope (JWST) program targeting HL Tau, focusing on the morphology and kinematics of the various wind components as well as on the water emission lines excited in the inner disk. James Webb Our observations with NIRSpec and MIRI cover the 1.66–28,μm spectral range, combining a 2times2 NIRSpec mosaic and a 2times(1times2) MIRI MRS mosaic to map the inner 10" of the redshifted lobe of the outflow and the base of the blueshifted lobe. We observe in the redshifted lobe a stratified wind composed of three nested layers: a fast, highly collimated atomic jet with an extrapolated geometrical radius at the base of 10 au and with an opening angle of ∼ 1degree, structured in a chain of eight knots separated by about 0 ; and with radial velocities of ∼ 160,km,s -1 -1 $, with an opening angle of ∼ 20degree that is asymmetric with respect to the axis and shows complex arc-like substructures; and a warm gas shell with a radial velocity of about 35̨ms that is visible in low-excitation transitions of CO ($ν=1-0). This CO (ν=1-0) shell is apparently cospatial with the CO (J=2-1) emission detected by ALMA with velocities of 3 to 25̨ms and appears as a distinct component from that detected in the disk. This component does not show substructures, and its properties suggest an origin from UV and/or IR pumping. The first 1arcsec of the blueshifted lobe shows a similar stratification, but the jet appears to be faster and less collimated, with a velocity of ∼ -175 ̨ms, an extrapolated geometrical radius at the base of 5 au, and an opening angle of ∼ 4 Additionally, the MIRI spectra taken at the star position show a rich forest of water lines that are dominated by cold-to-warm (łeq500,K) gas. The observed stratification and kinematics of the flow can support a magnetically driven disk-wind scenario in which the distinct components originate in the disk at progressively larger distances from the star. However, while the external components observed in CO have the laminar and regular appearance predicted for such winds, the knots in the inner jet and the arcs in the wind might be the manifestation of a pulsed ejection mechanism. The distribution of the water lines suggests an extended (possibly up to a radius of 26 au) reservoir of sublimated ices.

title: NGS-Based Insights into Population Differentiation and Genetic Baseline Development for Asian Coho Salmon
abstractText: Coho salmon, Oncorhynchus kisutch (Walbaum 1792), is a Pacific salmon species widely distributed across the North Pacific that supports commercial fisheries and hatchery enhancement programs. Within the Asian part of its range, coho salmon is the fourth most abundant species of the genus Oncorhynchus.

title: Thermal Conditions Control Size of East Kamchatka Pink Salmon Stock
abstractText: East Kamchatka (EK) pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) form one of the largest Pacific salmon stocks with a predominance of odd-year generations. Over the last 55 years, their catches have showed considerable variations both in odd and even years, from 18,830 metric tonnes in 1971 to 227,232 metric tonnes in 2019 and from 1,970 metric tonnes in 1972 to 111,261 metric tonnes in 2018, respectively (Fig. 1).

title: Investigating Sources of Ichthyophonus Infections in Yukon River Chinook Salmon
abstractText: The 3,190 km long transbound¬ary Yukon River that flows from Canada through Alaska supports one of the world’s largest subsistence salmon fisheries (Brown et al. 2021; Padilla et al. 2021). However, Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha, henceforth Chinook) from this river have continued to decline since 1998 (Ransbury et al. 2022). In most years since 2007, the abundance has been insufficient to meet escapement goals in both Alaska (U.S.) and Yukon (Canada), requiring harvest restrictions on both sides of the border, resulting in failure to provide for basic harvest needs (Joint Technical Committee [JTC] 2022). More recently there was a severe downturn of adult returns from 2019–2023 that reached a historic low in 2022 (DeFilippo et al. 2026). Although the reasons for the recent declines are unknown and likely multifaceted, studies in the early 2000s showed that low runs and up to 60% pre-spawning en route mortality were associated with severe, disseminated, ichthyophoniasis (Kocan and Hershberger 2001, 2006; Kocan et al. 2003, 2004). High en route mortality was again suspected as contributing to recent declines based on observations of approximately 45% fewer Canadian-origin Chinook enumerated at the Canadian border compared to assessment near the mouth of the Yukon River (JTC 2023).

title: Quantifying Environmental and Climate Drivers of Smolt-to-adult Survival in Okanagan Sockeye Salmon
abstractText: The recovery of Okanagan sockeye salmon since the late 1990s represents a notable success story at a time when many populations across the southern range of the species are in decline. This recovery has been attributed to a range of management actions, many led by the Okanagan Nation Alliance, targeting freshwater life stages, and to favourable marine conditions during this period (Alexander et al. 2024). Nevertheless, the causal links between these factors and productivity and survival have not been formally quantified. As a result, it remains difficult to incorporate these processes into ecosystem-based fisheries management and to assess the extent to which the factors underlying Okanagan sockeye recovery may be transferable to other populations.

title: Genomic Tools for Forecasting and Adaptive Management of Pink Salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) in the Sea of Okhotsk Basin
abstractText: Pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) is the most abundant species of Pacific salmon in Russia, and its catch volumes largely determine the overall outcome of the salmon fishing season. At the same time, this species is characterized by pronounced interannual fluctuations in abundance, both in the total size of adult returns and in the abundance of individual regional stocks. These fluctuations substantially complicate reliable forecasting, particularly in the Sea of Okhotsk basin. Traditionally, forecasts of adult returns have been based primarily on ichthyological data; however, in recent years, genetic methods have become increasingly important in stock assessment. Genetic stock identification (GSI) allows the proportional contributions of different regional stocks to be estimated to mixed Pacific salmon aggregations (Dann et al. 2013; Van Doornik et al. 2024). In many cases, modern GSI relies on the simultaneous analysis of hundreds or even thousands of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and depends on next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms for routine analysis (McKinney et al. 2022).

title: Variability of Korean Salmon Resources and Otolith Analysis of Returning Salmon
abstractText: Returns of Chum salmon (Oncorhynchus keta) to Korean rivers have shown pronounced interannual variability in abundance over recent decades. Although artificial propagation through hatchery production has been a central component of salmon resource management in Korea, quantitative field-based evidence demonstrating the contribution of hatchery-produced individuals to population recovery remains limited. This gap constrains objective evaluation and refinement of current management strategies.

title: A Common Low-Frequency Signal in Long-Term Body-Size Dynamics of Chum Salmon (Oncorhynchus keta) along Eastern Sakhalin (1991–2024)
abstractText: Declining body size in Pacific salmon is increasingly recognized as a pan-North Pacific phenomenon, yet quantitative assessments linking this trend to large-scale climate variability remain limited for northwestern Pacific stocks. We compiled a 34-year record (1991–2024) of fork length, body mass, and Fulton’s condition factor (K) for chum salmon (Oncorhynchus keta) from four fishing regions of eastern Sakhalin—Northeast Sakhalin, Terpeniya Bay, Southeast Sakhalin, and Aniva Bay (initial pooled dataset 81,700 individuals, pre-quality-control; final quality-controlled dataset: 296 year–region–age observation units, n = 69,955 fish). ANOVA confirmed significant inter-regional differences, with Northeast Sakhalin showing the largest body mass and length, and Aniva Bay the lowest mass and condition factor despite an intermediate fork length. Theil–Sen regression revealed a negative trend in all four regions, most pronounced in Northeast Sakhalin (−24.4 g/year), the only region in which the trend was statistically significant. Inter-regional Pearson correlation (r = 0.56–0.84) and wavelet coherence analysis identified a shared low-frequency signal at an 8–14-year periodicity. Lagged correlation and regression analysis linked this signal to the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (positive, 0–2-year lag) and, with a longer lag and opposite sign, to Niño 3.4 (negative, 3–4-year lag); climate predictors alone accounted for about 45% of interannual variance in body mass, rising to 54% once regional fixed effects were added. We conclude that chum salmon body-size decline along eastern Sakhalin is partly driven by a common, low-frequency climate signal operating at decadal scales, while the unexplained variance may reflect density-dependent effects, local oceanography, and hatchery practices, which a hatchery-based dataset cannot fully separate from the climate signal.

title: Acoustically-Derived Distribution and Abundance Estimates of Salmon and their Prey in the North Pacific Ocean in Winter as Observed by the 2022 IYS Pan-Pacific Expedition
abstractText: Although winter has been hypothesized to constitute a “survival bottleneck” for the oceanic life-history phase of Pacific salmon species due to presumed low prey availability, oceanic winter conditions remain a black box in understanding salmon ecology (Myers et al. 2016). During February/March of the 2022 International Year of the Salmon (IYS) Pan-Pacific Expedition, science vessels from Canada, the U.S., and Russia collected multifrequency echosounder backscatter data along their survey tracks. Using advanced backscattering partitioning models we quantified the distribution of salmon and the major mesopelagic and micronektonic taxa in the North Pacific Ocean at a higher spatial resolution than previously achieved.

title: Low HbA1c as a sign of increased erythrocyte turnover
Pink Salmon Adaptation to the Warming Climate: Smaller but Stronger?
abstractText: Pink salmon continue to predominate in the total Pacific salmon run reaching 68.4% of total salmon numbers and 53.5% of biomass in commercial catches in 2025. In many recent publications, pink salmon are considered a successful competitor in the North Pacific pelagic fish community, which are well adapted to climate warming and resilient to heat waves (Ruggerone et al. 2021; Rand and Ruggerone 2024). Salmon of four other species suffer from a warming ocean, reduced food supply, and competition, which results in a decline in adult fish size. Large-sized species such as chum and Chinook salmon are impacted to the highest degree (Oke et al. 2020).

title: Weakening of the Cold Oyashio Current Intrusion Causes Low Early Growth Rate and Poor Adult Return of Chum Salmon Along the Northeastern Coast of Honshu, Japan
abstractText: The waters along the northeastern coast of Honshu, Japan, are characterized by dynamic fluctuations influenced by the cold Oyashio Current and the warm Kuroshio Extension Current. The Oyashio and Kuroshio are western boundary currents of the subarctic and subtropical circulations of the North Pacific Ocean, respectively. The subarctic circulation flowing from the coast of Alaska moves westward along the southern side of the Aleutian Islands. After leaving the Aleutian Islands (and rejoining part of the current from the Bering Sea), it flows southeastward along the eastern coast of the Kamchatka Peninsula and eventually reaches the east coast of Honshu. This cold current flowing along the east coast of Honshu is known as the first Oyashio intrusion, and its southern boundary is defined as the 5°C isotherm at a depth of 100 m (Qiu 2019). The strength of the Oyashio southward intrusion is indicated by the latitude of this southern boundary, where a relatively high latitude indicates a weak intrusion and a low latitude, a strong one. The southernmost latitude of the Oyashio Current intrusion exhibits strong year-to-year fluctuation and has been moving poleward since the 1990s (Fig. 1). A recent study has shown that the Kuroshio-originating warm core eddy, which obstructs the Oyashio southward intrusion, strongly affects the strength of the Oyashio intrusion along the east coast of Honshu (Okunishi et al. 2024).

title: Long-term Dynamics for Some Biological Parameters of Pink Salmon from Asiatic Herds
abstractText: The northern North Pacific is warming, and Pacific salmon abundance is now at its highest level in the past century. Recent years, however, have seen a downward trend in salmon catches (NPAFC Statistics: Pacific Salmonid Catch and Hatchery Release Data https://www.npafc.org/statistics/). Concurrently with long-term catch dynamics, changes in salmon productivity—especially for pink salmon—are becoming apparent. Many researchers have noted a decrease in the body size and weight and growth rate of salmon during periods of high abundance (Ishida et al. 1993; Welch and Morris 1994; Bigler et al. 1996; Kaeriyama 1998, 2003; Volobuev and Volobuev 2000; Kaev 2003; Lagunov 2004; Sviridov et al. 2004; Zavolokin et al. 2008, 2012; and many others). Despite significant scientific efforts and the considerable progress achieved in understanding pink salmon biology, opinions among researchers regarding the causes of its size fluctuations remain deeply conflicting, and the search for causal relationships underlying these changes is still far from complete.

title: The Century-Long Dynamics of Stocks and Average Body Weight of Pacific Salmon in the Russian Far East through the Prism of Climate Cycles and Trends
abstractText: The complex pattern of variations in the thermal characteristics of the environment surrounding Pacific salmon, including the linear positive trend and periodic changes for an 80-year cycle, has been elucidated. A positive relationship was found between the dynamics of pink, chum, and sockeye salmon harvest and the general vector of variations in the temperature background. The full cycle periods in the population dynamics of pink, chum, sockeye, coho, and Chinook salmon are expected to also last about 80 years, while the cycles of pink, chum, and sockeye salmon are synchronized with temperature extrema. The dynamics of Chinook salmon catches occur in antiphase to those of pink, chum, and sockeye salmon. The extrema for coho salmon abundance are shifted 20–25 years ahead of the extrema for pink, chum, and sockeye salmon and are approximately 15 years ahead of the extrema for Chinook salmon. It is assumed that the maximum of average catches of the common Pacific salmon species (pink, chum, and sockeye salmon) in the current cycle already passed by the early 2020s.The reduction in average catches of Russian Pacific salmon may last until the 2050s, will be higher than the previous minimum, and will reach the level of average annual catches of approximately 250,000 mt. During the 70–100-year warming period, as confirmed by ichthyological studies, Chinook salmon has “lost” up to 60% of the average body weight of individuals, while chum, sockeye, and coho salmon have lost up to 25–30%. The average body weight of pink salmon depends on the abundance of individuals feeding together, especially in years when extra-strong year-classes are formed, rather than on variations in ambient temperature.

title: Developing A Refined View of High Seas Pacific Salmon Distributions Through Machine Learning
abstractText: The oceanic habitat conditions that Pacific salmon encounter during the pelagic life stage have a substantial effect on their distribution, growth, and survival. Fisheries and monitoring data collected in coastal marine and freshwater areas are often linked to conditions in oceanic habitat to attempt to explain patterns in salmon population productivity as their marine rearing habitats continue to change (Connors et al. 2020; Kitada et al. 2025; Ohlberger et al. 2025). However, a substantial source of uncertainty in such analyses stems from knowledge gaps regarding the habitats that salmon utilize while at sea. For this reason, many research efforts have worked to characterize the oceanic ranges of each species and how they relate to environmental factors like sea surface temperature (e.g., Abdul-Aziz et al. 2011; Langan et al. 2024; Alabia et al. 2025). Yet, these characterizations often present a coarse view of salmon distributions generated through summarizing or smoothing catch data over large spatial scales. In order to address contemporary challenges to salmon management, such as evaluating if and where/when high seas competition among species may take place (Ruggerone et al. 2023) or enhancing the effectiveness of enforcement activities against Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing, new approaches are needed to maximize the spatiotemporal insight gained from composite historical datasets.

title: Serological findings of the population-based Hamburg City Health Study
Enhanced Biological Pumping at Submesoscale Edge Fronts
abstractText: The northern Norwegian Sea is a key gateway for transporting heat, nutrients, and biomass from the Atlantic toward the Arctic Ocean. Although submesoscale dynamics are recognized as important regulators of regional ecosystem structure, their role in sustaining persistently high biomass remains poorly understood. By integrating five years of Seaglider observations with more than two decades of biogeochemical station data, we identify intense vertical motions concentrated along mesoscale eddy edges. These motions have horizontal scales below 10 km and extend to depths of at least 500 m. Observations and dynamical diagnostics indicate that they are generated by submesoscale secondary circulations associated with geostrophic strain. During the spring bloom and Calanus finmarchicus swarm seasons, these circulations transport nutrients from the ocean interior toward the surface. The resulting nutrient-rich rings support elevated phytoplankton and zooplankton biomass, highlighting the ecological importance of submesoscale eddy-edge fronts in the northern Norwegian Sea.

title: Cumulative Stressors and Climate-driven Variability Shape Upper Fraser River Chinook Salmon Dynamics
abstractText: Upper Fraser River (UFR) Spring 52 Chinook Salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) comprise two Designatable Units (DUs) spawning throughout the middle and upper Fraser River watershed. Both experienced substantial declines in abundance over recent decades and were assessed as Threatened (DU9) and Endangered (DU11) in 2019. More recently, abundance has increased in both DUs (Fig. 1), although populations remain below historical levels and uncertainty remains regarding their long-term recovery. Their complex life history exposes them to a diverse suite of stressors across natal watersheds, the Fraser River migration corridor and estuary, and nearshore and offshore marine environments.

title: Integrating Salmonid Thermal Niches into Subarctic Pacific Ecosystem Models Improves Hindcast Simulation Performance
abstractText: Pacific salmonids (Oncorhynchus spp.) spend the pelagic phases of their life cycles in open subarctic waters. These ecosystems are therefore considered crucial to the growth and survival of these species, which are of vital ecological, economic, and cultural importance to North Pacific countries. In recent decades, both interdecadal ocean warming and interannual marine heatwaves have occurred in the open subarctic Pacific. These oceanographic phenomena could adversely impact salmon directly (i.e., through physiological stress from temperatures exceeding thermal optima) and indirectly (i.e., through altered primary productivity and/or the quantity and/or quality of prey zooplankton and micronekton). Thus, understanding the impacts of climate change and variability on salmon biomass is highly important to NPAFC member states.

title: Freshwater Landlocked Chinook Salmon Behaviour and Use of Habitat Diverge from Source Populations in the Pacific Region—Cross-System Science for a Changing Native Range
abstractText: Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) are a keystone species for ecological stability with substantial socio-economic benefits across the Northern Hemisphere. In their native Pacific range, they serve as a major source of marine-derived nutrients for marine-connected fluvial ecosystems, support multi-billion dollar commercial and recreational industries (Quinn 2005), and are an iconic species in Indigenous cultures (Nesbitt and Moore 2016). Chinook salmon have assumed a similar role in the Laurentian Great Lakes following their successful introduction in the late 1960s (Crawford and Muir 2008) as a top predator to control non-native alewife (Alosa pseudoharengus) (Tanner and Tody 2002) and to support a multi-billion dollar recreational fishery (Melstrom and Lupi 2013; The Great Lakes Valuation Report 2022). This dual economic and ecological importance makes them a focal point in both regions for management decisions, especially given the current declines of some of the species stocks in the Pacific region (Ford 2022; Atlas et al. 2023).

title: Life-History Specific Survival Rates for Natural Origin Chinook Salmon
abstractText: Not every Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) is the same, and within every population there are inherited traits that maximize fitness for the conditions faced within their unique context. These traits are known as life-history traits. Subyearling, or ocean-type, Chinook salmon can exemplify one of multiple phenotypes at emigration from the river, with the two most common being fry and parr. Within the Sarita River on the West Coast of Vancouver Island, 96.5% of out-migrating Chinook salmon leave the river as fry and 3.5% as parr, but it is unclear how these two life-history types contribute to the adult population. We looked at using otolith microchemistry to identify the size at estuary entry of successfully returning adult Chinook salmon to the Sarita River. We found that fry only contributed 62.1% of the adult returns with a smolt-to-adult survival rate of 0.08% (95% CI: 0.01 – 0.33%), while parr contributed to 37.9% of the adult returns with a smolt-to-adult survival rate of 1.23% (95% CI: 0.27 – 4.00). We also found that the majority of the survival differences between fry and parr occurred early on as the contributions to the post-smolts was similar to the adults, but not to the out-migrating smolts. Our findings suggest that excess natural origin Chinook salmon mortalities may be occurring due to limited freshwater rearing habitat.

title: Freshwater Hydrology Emerges as the Strongest Predictor of Phenological Variability in a Southeast Alaska Steelhead Trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) Population
abstractText: Phenological variation, such as the migration trends of salmonids, may provide resilience in changing environmental scenarios, influencing individual survival and population productivity. However, phenologies have shifted on a global scale, and at an unprecedented rate, over the past few decades due to environmental change (Kharouba et al. 2018), with temperature and precipitation emerging as two widespread drivers (Cohen et al. 2018). Phenological shifts may be particularly consequential for anadromous species that rely on seasonal cues for migration between freshwater and marine habitats. Steelhead trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), the anadromous life history variant of rainbow trout, may be particularly sensitive to phenological changes due to the complexity of their life history, including the occurrence of two highly distinct life history variants, the possibility of iteroparity, and the wide range of habitats occupied.

title: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) Deficiency in Pacific Salmon Illustrates the Need for Continued Ecosystem Research
abstractText: Thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency is a conservation issue affecting Pacific salmon (Oncorhynchus spp.) through elevated fry mortality and sublethal effects across their lifecycle. Salmon require thiamine for basic cellular metabolism and must acquire it through dietary sources. Without sufficient thiamine, they experience cardiovascular and neurological problems, impaired immune response and migration, and lower growth rate and survival (reviewed by Harder et al. 2018). The effects of low thiamine are also maternally transferred because developing eggs and yolk-sac fry rely on thiamine deposited in eggs from maternal stores, and without enough they cannot survive. Thiamine deficiency was first identified in the Pacific Ocean in Chinook salmon in Alaska in 2012 and 2014 (Honeyfield et al. 2016; Larson and Howard 2019). It was subsequently reported in California Central Valley Chinook salmon in 2020 (Mantua et al. 2021, 2025), and most recently coho salmon and steelhead in Oregon and California (Reed et al. 2023; Mantua et al. 2025). In British Columbia (BC), Welch et al. (2018) measured thiamine concentrations in salmon sampled in 2015 and found no evidence of thiamine deficiency. However, more recent sampling revealed thiamine-deficient eggs in eight BC Chinook salmon populations sampled during 2023 and 2024 (Lerner et al. in prep), suggesting that thiamine deficiency may now be more widespread in Pacific salmon populations than previously recognized.

title: Capabilities Required from a Digital Twin of a Salmon’s Life
abstractText: A salmon digital twin is a data-driven simulation model of a salmon population, fitted to historical data and kept up-to-date. It can consist of linked virtual representations of successive life stages—twins for returning adults, eggs, parr, etc.—that pass information between stages as new observations become available. This provides visibility of the current and predicted states, including predictions from “What If?” scenarios. Translating environmental data into indices of how a habitat affects the salmon experiencing that habitat requires corresponding habitat twins. Improved awareness of what is happening to a salmon population allows improved decisions: strategies for revitalization, tactics for response to disasters. To be valuable and effective, the decision support products (scenarios, reports, infographics) from a salmon twin will differ across the agencies and user-groups involved. We summarize our guidelines by saying a salmon digital twin should be USER-friendly: Understandable, Safe, Effective, and Reusable.

title: Salmon Domains; A New Perspective on Oceanic Distributions of Pacific Salmon
abstractText: The oceanic distributions of salmon species, of regional stocks, or of populations have often been represented by their ranges, i.e., lines on maps encompassing the extremes of a distribution. Ranges were often determined from high seas tagging, for resolutions finer than species. Unfortunately, this representation of distribution provides no indication of the variation in abundance within the encircled range. The present study used catch per unit effort (CPUE) data to examine the relative abundance of species across the salmosphere to focus on defining regions where species tend to be most abundant. Perhaps where they were most abundant is more appropriate as little sampling has been conducted offshore in recent decades, although winter sampling during the International Year of the Salmon (IYS) in 2022 was qualitatively similar to winter sampling in the winter of 1964 (Manzer and Dodimead 1965).

title: Enhanced Performance of Fiber Optic Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) Sensor Using a Hybrid TiO2- CQDs Layer
abstractText: This study aims to design and investigate the performance of a fiber-optic Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) sensor utilizing a hybrid dielectric layer composed of Titanium dioxide (TiO₂) and Carbon Quantum Dots (CQDs) coated on a thin gold (Au) film. The Au–TiO₂–CQDs hybrid design was applied to optimize sensor performance by examining the relationship between layer surface roughness and optical response. Variation in CQDs deposition time on the TiO₂ layer was used as a parameter to evaluate its effect on the morphology of the sensor layer. The characterization results showed that increasing the CQDs deposition time decreased the layer’s surface roughness, significantly impacting the sensor's optical response, particularly by decreasing the transmittance and Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) values on the SPR curve. Performance testing using variations in the refractive index of ethanol showed an increase in sensitivity from 2243.06 nm/RIU (on a single Au layer) to 3721.14 nm/RIU (for the optimized Au–TiO₂–CQDs hybrid layer). This improvement is attributed to the morphological modification of the porous structure of TiO₂ and CQDs, which directly affects the optical mechanism and enhances plasmonic interaction at the metal–dielectric interface. This finding confirms that controlling the surface roughness of dielectric layers such as TiO₂ through surface modification and the integration of quantum dots nanomaterials is an effective strategy for improving plasmonic interaction and overall performance of fiber-optic SPR sensors.

title: Synergistic Strengthening of A713 Alloy with FeNb Reinforcement on Mechanical and Microstructural Characteristics
abstractText: This research study investigates the hardness, tensile strength, and microstructural characteristics of A713 alloy reinforced with ferroniobium (FeNb) at 0, 2, 4, and 6 wt.% levels. A713 MMCs were synthesized using electromagnetic stir-casting and analyzed through tensile testing, hardness testing, optical microscopy, SEM with EDS, and X-ray diffraction. ASTM standards were followed for tensile and hardness measurements. Adding FeNb significantly enhanced the composite's mechanical properties by refining the grain structure and strengthening load-bearing capabilities. The A713-6wt.% FeNb composite exhibited the highest tensile strength (222.20 MPa) and Vickers hardness (129.37 HV), outperforming the base alloy (184.14 MPa, 97.13 HV). This represents an improvement of 33.19% in hardness and 20.66% in tensile strength. SEM analysis of the A713 alloy revealed α-Al dendrites and Al 2 Zn intermetallic compounds, while the A713-6wt.% FeNb composite displayed these features alongside Fe 2 Nb phases. XRD analysis confirmed the presence of these phases, and SEM images showed Fe 2 Nb phases uniformly distributed across intermetallic compounds. The addition of FeNb reduced inter-dendritic separation, promoted grain boundary interlocking, and produced a homogenous microstructure, improving strength. This study demonstrates that FeNb reinforcement enhances the mechanical and morphological behavior of A713 alloys, making them appropriate for essential-performance automobile and aerospace applications requiring superior strength and hardness.

title: State of Art Investigation of Modified Polymer Matrix Reinforced with Multiwall Nanofillers
abstractText: Monolithic materials are not always met the technological demands of the present era therefore to meet the technological needs different materials merged together. Present work is focused to analyze the effective characterization of polymer matrix composite and reinforced multi walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) in the polymer. Modified polymer matrix composite is the combination of bisphenol epoxy (C 21 H 24 O 4), hardener and MWCNT in desired percentage. The epoxy and hardener ratio are maintained at 10:1. Nanocomposites are prepared by shear mixing of epoxy and MWCNT. Ultrasonication and magnetic stirring were utilized for dumbbell and rectangular shaped sample preparation as per ASTM standard. The multiwall CNT is added in polymer matrix in a varying wt. percentage of 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 %. The effect of nano filler addition was investigated by tensile testing on Instron UTM. The result shows that the composition with the addition of MWCNT and carbon fiber is having high elastic strength and force carrying capacity as compared to polymer matrix composite with MWCNT. The maximum tensile strength is noted for the sample with 0.5% of MWCNT content. The mechanical properties drop for the sample with content of 0.7% MWCNT which denotes agglomeration. The ply orientation of carbon fibre is also varied to study the effect of tensile loading. The variation in aspect ratio is also made to check the effect of change in geometrical properties on load carrying capacity of specimen.
