title: The Role of Hydrazine Concentration in Optimizing the Electrical and Structural Properties rGO Films-Based Glucose Biosensors
abstractText: The concentration of hydrazine, used as a reducing agent, significantly affects the properties of reduced graphene oxide (rGO) when employed as an active layer in glucose sensors. Hydrazine plays a key role in reducing graphene oxide (GO) to rGO, thereby enhancing its electrical conductivity by removing oxygen functional groups. In this study, rGO was deposited onto a working electrode using a spin-coating method to achieve a thin, homogeneous, stable, and well-controlled film. The concentration of hydrazine hydrate was varied at 0.1 mL, 0.3 mL, and 0.5 mL for every 5 mL of GO solution. The fabricated films were then characterized using an Optical Microscopy (OM) to observe film uniformity, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) to analyze surface morphology, a Topography Measurement System (TMS) to determine film thickness, a JG Four-Probe Resistivity Tester to measure electrical conductivity, and a PicoScope 5000 Series for impedance analysis. The results show that increasing the hydrazine concentration produces rGO films with improved homogeneity, higher thickness, and greater electrical conductivity due to more effective reduction of oxygen groups. FTIR spectra confirmed the removal of oxygen functionalities, while SEM revealed wrinkle-like structures that enhance the electroactive surface area. Impedance measurements indicated capacitive behavior, demonstrating efficient charge transfer across the rGO/electrolyte interface. Therefore, hydrazine-reduced rGO exhibits excellent potential as an active electrode material for developing sensitive and stable non-enzymatic glucose biosensors.

title: First-Principles Investigation of Electronic Interaction and Optical Modulation in Silicene Quantum Dots upon CO and NO Adsorption
abstractText: In this study, the structural, electronic, and optical properties of silicene quantum dots (SiQD) before and after CO and NO adsorption were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) within the Quantum ESPRESSO framework. The optimized structures show that gas adsorption does not destroy the SiQD framework but induces local changes in bond lengths and adsorption distances. The band structure and density of states analysis indicate that SiQD retains its semiconducting nature, while the QDSi-NO system exhibits new states near the Fermi level, suggesting stronger electronic interaction compared to QDSi-CO. The HOMO-LUMO analysis, charge density difference, and Bader charge calculations reveal that charge transfer increases from CO to NO, with NO causing charge redistribution over several Si atoms. Optical results show that the main JDOS peak of pristine QDSi at about 6.5 eV shifts to the 3-4 eV range after adsorption, with a strong peak at approximately 3.7 eV in the QDSi-NO system. The absorption spectra and dielectric function indicate significant modulation in the low and medium energy regions after NO adsorption, while CO causes only slight intensity changes. These findings suggest that SiQD is a promising material for gas sensing applications, especially for NO detection, with the ability to modulate both electrical and optical signals.

title: Photocatalytic Degradation of Safranine and Bromocresol Green Dyes in Water Using CuBiS2 Nanoparticles
abstractText: The persistence of synthetic dyes in industrial wastewater poses a significant environmental challenge due to their toxicity, stability, and resistance to conventional treatment methods. This study investigates the synthesis of copper bismuth sulphide (CuBiS₂) nanoparticles as a visible-light-responsive photocatalyst for the degradation of Safranine (SE) and Bromocresol Green (BG) dyes in water. The CuBiS₂ nanoparticles were synthesised using N -methyl- N -ethanol dithiocarbamato complexes of Bi(III) and Cu(II) as single precursor compounds under an inert atmosphere. The product was characterised using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and UV-vis spectroscopy. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of a crystalline orthorhombic CuBiS₂ phase, while microscopic analysis revealed that the CuBiS₂ nanoparticles exhibited a predominantly rod-shaped morphology. UV-vis showed strong absorption in the visible region with a band gap of approximately 2.20 eV, indicating high potential for solar-driven photocatalysis. Photocatalytic experiments conducted under visible light demonstrated significant degradation efficiencies of 97.2% for Safranine and 85% for Bromocresol Green after 120 and 180 min of irradiation, respectively, at a concentration of 25 mg/L. The performance is attributed to the narrow bandgap and high absorption in the visible range of CuBiS₂. However, the higher degradation efficiency of SE observed over a shorter reaction time may indicate a greater interaction between CuBiS₂ nanoparticles and SE. The results suggest that CuBiS₂ nanoparticles may be a promising alternative to commercial photocatalysts for treating dye-contaminated wastewater.

title: Study on the Synthesis of Zn2+- Doped CsPbBr3 Quantum Dots by Microfluidic Method and Their Luminescence Properties
abstractText: In this work, we adopted a microfluidic-assisted synthesis strategy to address the critical challenges of poor doping homogeneity, large batch-to-batch variation, and insufficient luminescent performance of CsPbBr₃ perovskite quantum dots (QDs) fabricated by conventional batch synthesis. A Y-junction combined with serpentine microchannel was designed and optimized via multiphysics field simulation, achieving rapid and homogeneous mixing of precursor solutions for controllable fabrication of Zn²⁺-doped CsPbBr₃ QDs. Experimental results show that the QDs with an optimized Zn/Pb molar ratio of 2:1 deliver a high photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 82.9% and a significantly prolonged exciton lifetime from 8.56 ns to 22.28 ns, with the emission wavelength tuned from green to cyan region via bandgap modulation. Structural characterizations confirm homogeneous Zn²⁺ incorporation into the perovskite lattice without phase separation, accompanied by lattice contraction. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal the mechanism of bandgap widening and electronic state contribution from Zn orbitals. Notably, quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs) fabricated with the optimized doped QDs as the emission layer achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.4% and a maximum luminance of 50324 cd/m², demonstrating outstanding practical application potential. This work provides a scalable and controllable approach for synthesizing high-performance perovskite QDs toward optoelectronic applications.

title: Morphometric Study of the Length and Breadth of the Hip Bone in the Bangladeshi Population
abstractText: Background: Hip bone morphology varies across populations and provides useful information for anthropology, forensic identification, and clinical anatomy. Population-specific osteometric data on hip bone length and breadth remain limited in Bangladesh. Objective: To determine the length and breadth of dry adult human hip bones in a Bangladeshi population, compare these measurements according to anatomical side, and assess the relationship between hip bone length and breadth. Methods: This descriptive morphometric study included 150 dry adult human hip bones, comprising 82 right-sided and 68 left-sided specimens, obtained from the Departments of Anatomy of Mymensingh Medical College and Community Based Medical College, Mymensingh, Bangladesh. Hip bone length and breadth were measured in centimeters using standard osteometric methods. Data were summarized as range, mean, and standard deviation. Pearson correlation was used to assess the relationship between length and breadth on the right and left sides. A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Right hip bone length ranged from 16.7 to 22.0 cm, with a mean of 19.45 ± 1.03 cm, while left hip bone length ranged from 16.8 to 22.0 cm, with a mean of 19.47 ± 1.18 cm. Breadth ranged from 13.0 to 16.2 cm on both sides. The mean breadth was 14.19 ± 0.69 cm on the right side and 14.44 ± 0.82 cm on the left side. A significant positive correlation was observed between length and breadth on the right side (r = 0.376, p = 0.001) and left side (r = 0.436, p = 0.010). Conclusion: This study provides baseline morphometric reference data for hip bone length and breadth in the Bangladeshi population. Both dimensions showed slight left-sided dominance and significant positive bilateral correlations. These findings may be useful for comparative anatomy, population-specific osteometric databases, forensic anthropology, and skeletal identification.

title: Electronic and Structural Properties of Ca: Zr Co-Doped Hexagonal BaTiO3
abstractText: The main objective of this research is to study the electronic and morphological properties of hexagonal BaTiO 3 polymorph. Crystal structure and electronic properties of hexagonal phase of BaTiO 3 perovskite, Ca:Zr doped BaTiO 3 (BCZT) are explored using both generalized gradient (GGA) and GGA+U approximation within the density functional theory (DFT) framework . Pristine hexagonal BaTiO 3 shows a severely underestimated bandgap of 1.84 eV when we only employ a GGA approximation. This is further corrected by using GGA+U where the direct bandgap is found to increase to 3.42 eV, which is in good agreement with experimental and other theoretical studies of 3.38 eV (which have employed hybrid functionals). Upon co-doing BaTiO 3 with Ca and Zr, we find that the direct bandgap of the system increases to 3.64 eV. The bandgap values computed using GGA+U are consistent with other theoretical findings from other BaTiO 3 polymorphs. In addition, the wide bandgap observed in BCZT, along with the shifting of the conduction and valence bands away from the Fermi level, shows an increased bandgap of 3.64 eV. This minimizes leakage currents making BCZT a promising material for piezoelectric applications.

title: Core/Shell Nanoparticle Modified Ethyl Silicate Consolidants for the Conservation of Heritage Limestone: Mechanical Reinforcement, Water Resistance, and Microstructural Stability
abstractText: Heritage limestone structures are continuously threatened by moisture infiltration, salt crystallization, thermal cycling, biological colonization, and atmospheric pollutants. Conventional consolidants including acrylic polymers, nanolime, and plain ethyl silicates offer only partial protection, limited by inadequate substrate compatibility, insufficient mechanical reinforcement, or irreversibility concerns. The present study investigates the performance of three core/shell nanostructures SiO₂/CaCO₃, TiO₂/CaCO₃, and ZnO/CaCO₃ loaded into SILRES® BS OH 100 ethyl silicate consolidant for Mokattam limestone sourced from the same quarry as the historic Sabil of Umm Muhammad Ali Al-Saghir, Cairo. Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis established that the limestone possesses a mesoporous architecture with a multipoint surface area of 28.87 m²/g, total pore volume of 0.19–0.26 cm³/g, and average pore radii of 2.0–2.4 nm. These parameters guided the calculation of optimal consolidant loading concentrations: SiO₂/CaCO₃ at 0.15 g/100 mL, TiO₂/CaCO₃ at 0.18 g/100 mL, and ZnO/CaCO₃ at 0.22 g/100 mL. All nanoparticles exhibited hydrodynamic diameters below 100 nm (DLS: 58, 42, and 51 nm, respectively) and zeta potentials below −30 mV (−31, −33, and −36 mV), confirming excellent colloidal stability. Core/shell architecture was confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscope (TEM), scanning electron microscope (SEM), and atomic force microscope (AFM) analyses. Treated specimens underwent accelerated thermal ageing (EN 14066: 50 cycles, 70 °C/20 °C) and salt crystallization ageing (EN 12370: 15 cycles, 15% NaCl). Post treatment evaluation demonstrated significant improvements: compressive strength increased by 77% for SiO₂/CaCO₃ + SILRES (8,595 kgf vs. 4,855 kgf untreated), by 36% for ZnO/CaCO₃ + SILRES (6,607 kgf), and by 14% for TiO₂/CaCO₃ + SILRES (5,552 kgf). Water absorption decreased from 10.99% to 9.50%, 9.90%, and 10.04% respectively. Colorimetric analysis yielded mean ΔE₀₀ values of 2.80, 1.50, and 4.10, all within accepted conservation thresholds (ΔE₀₀ < 5). FTIR and XRD confirmed preservation of the calcite framework after ageing. SEM demonstrated improved intergranular cohesion while maintaining stone breathability. The BET guided dosing strategy, combining quantitative pore analysis with core/shell nanoparticle engineering, represents a novel and reproducible evidence based methodology for heritage limestone conservation.

title: Microwave Sintering of ZrB₂-TiC Composites: Microstructural Evolution and Mechanical Properties
abstractText: Zirconium diboride (ZrB 2) possesses distinct combination of physical, mechanical and thermal characteristics, rendering it ideal for a range of applications, including leading edges and nose caps of hypersonic spacecraft, missile cones and refractory crucibles. However, its lower fracture toughness and vulnerability to oxidation attributed to its covalent bonding nature, restrict its practical utility under severe service conditions. Thus, the study examined the effect of incorporating 10-30 vol.% TiC on densification, microstructure and mechanical behavior of ZrB 2 -TiC composites sintered using microwave sintering. The addition of 0.5 vol. % Ni as a sintering aid improved the densification at lower sintering temperature. The incorporation of TiC improved the sinterability, Vickers hardness, fracture toughness and compressive strength owing to (Ti,Zr)C and (Zr,Ti)B 2 solid solutions formation. The composite containing 20 vol.% TiC demonstrated the maximum Vickers hardness of 21.8 GPa and a compressive strength of 1544 MPa owing to enhanced densification and greater TiC dispersion within the ZrB 2 matrix. The maximum fracture toughness of 5.1 MPa.m 0.5 was attained at 30 vol.% TiC, primarily due to toughening mechanisms such as TiC particle pull out and crack deflection. The developed composites could be potentially utilized for extreme high-temperature aerospace applications like rocket nozzles, leading edges, and nose caps for next-generation aircraft carriers.

title: A qualitative study of pre-arrival nervousness among postgraduate taught students entering a United Kingdom university
abstractText: Purpose Postgraduate taught (PGT) study is often assumed to follow seamlessly from undergraduate education. However, the transition represents a distinct and potentially anxiety-provoking life change. This study aims to explore pre-arrival nervousness among incoming PGT students at a United Kingdom university. Design/methodology/approach Of 1,964 eligible students across 12 academic schools, 1,332 completed an online survey. Qualitative analysis drew on 627 responses to an open-ended question inviting reflections on concerns about starting a PGT study, with responses that were not relevant to the question or left unanswered excluded from analysis. Findings Findings revealed interconnected transitional anxieties relating to academic preparedness and workload expectations, cultural and environmental adjustment, social integration and communication, financial pressures, wellbeing and health, administrative uncertainty and separation from family. Originality/value Interpreted through Schlossberg’s Transition Theory, students’ concerns reflected appraisals of their situation and of themselves, whereas support and coping strategies were largely anticipated rather than available or enacted. The findings position the pre-arrival phase as an under-examined stage of PGT transition and suggest potential areas for proactive, targeted institutional support.

title: TECHNOLOGICAL MATURITY AND INDUSTRIAL TRAJECTORIES OF ENHANCED OIL RECOVERY TECHNOLOGIES: EVIDENCE FROM FOUR DECADES OF SCIENTIFIC DEVELOPMENT
abstractText: Enhanced oil recovery (EOR) technologies have diversified substantially over the last four decades, creating a heterogeneous technological landscape in which scientific activity and industrial implementation do not necessarily evolve in parallel. This study evaluates the technological evolution and industrial maturity of major EOR technologies between 1986 and 2026 through a bibliometric analysis of the Lens database. A total of 188,138 records were initially retrieved using 30 complementary search strategies covering technological families, development stages, implementation pathways, and adoption barriers. After hierarchical deduplication and two successive thematic filtering stages (EOR 1.0 and EOR 2.0), a final corpus of 24,327 publications was obtained. Documents were classified into sixteen EOR technologies and five maturity stages ranging from laboratory validation (M1) to sustained industrial maturity (M5). Results show that Thermal EOR (40.87%), in-situ combustion (40.42%), ASP (34.26%), MEOR (32.85%), WAG (30.17%), CO₂-EOR (29.71%) and polymer flooding (29.59%) exhibit the highest Industrial Maturity Share (M3–M5), indicating stronger evidence of operational validation and commercial implementation. In contrast, nanotechnology (14.66%), low-salinity waterflooding (16.29%) and hybrid methods (14.04%) remain predominantly associated with experimental stages. Overall, industrial maturity was found to depend less on scientific activity intensity than on the accumulation of documented operational evidence and successful field deployment over time.

title: A new chapter: Clinical Psychology in Europe moves on
Addressing treatment non-response: A pilot study of inhibitory retrieval–focused exposure therapy
abstractText: Background Inhibitory retrieval (IR-) focused exposure treatment may help overcome treatment non-response in anxiety disorders. However, evidence of its feasibility, acceptance, and effectiveness in this crucial patient group is lacking. Method We successfully re-invited patients with spider phobia who had not responded to the previous virtual reality exposure therapy (SpiderVR study) and responders. Additionally, we recruited healthy controls. Non-responders underwent an IR-focused one-session in vivo exposure with two conditions, i.e., with and without additional affect labeling. Pre- and post- treatment and at a 6-month follow-up, participants underwent clinical assessment, including self-reported symptom severity and a behavioral avoidance test. Applying multilevel models, we examined the feasibility, acceptance, and effectiveness. Exploratively, we described individual long-term trajectories. Results The additional IR-focused exposure produced lasting reductions in cognitive and behavioral symptoms in non-responders, with high adherence and acceptance rates. Additional affect labeling during IR-focused exposure had no effect. No associations were found with process variables related to potential mechanisms of change. Conclusion These findings suggest that implementing IR-focused exposure is feasible and well-received, offering clinical benefits to non-responders. Results underscore the need for further longitudinal research to optimize therapy for this critical patient group.

title: Divergent profiles of trait emotional intelligence in depression, anxiety, and insomnia
abstractText: Background Trait emotional intelligence (trait EI) has been linked to mental health outcomes, but little is known about disorder-specific emotional profiles in clinical populations. Identifying such profiles may inform transdiagnostic models and tailored interventions. Method In this cross-sectional study, we compared trait EI across individuals with depression (n = 200), anxiety-related disorders (n = 61), or insomnia (n = 47) and matched non-clinical controls (N = 608 total). All participants completed the Trait Emotional Intelligence Questionnaire – Short Form (TEIQue-SF). Group differences were examined for the global score and four subscales (Well-being, Self-control, Emotionality, Sociability). Results All clinical groups scored significantly lower than their respective controls on the TEIQue-SF global score and all subscales (all p s < .001). Between clinical groups, disorder-specific patterns emerged: Individuals with depression scored lower than those with insomnia on global trait EI and Well-being, reflecting diminished positive affect and life satisfaction. The insomnia group showed higher Self-control scores than the depression and anxiety groups, though the insomnia–anxiety difference was attenuated after controlling for age. No other significant differences were found between clinical groups. Conclusion Findings highlight robust trait EI deficits across depression, anxiety, and insomnia, alongside disorder-specific patterns in Well-being and Self-control. These results emphasize the need to consider demographic factors and emotional competencies in clinical research and give some indication that trait EI may be a promising target for transdiagnostic assessment and intervention.

title: MAPPING THE GLOBAL EVOLUTION OF ENHANCED OIL RECOVERY TECHNOLOGIES: SCIENTIFIC SPECIALIZATION, KNOWLEDGE INTEGRATION, AND PATENT INFLUENCE
abstractText: This study mapped the scientific and technological evolution of enhanced oil recovery (EOR) by integrating technological structure, geographical distribution, specialization, institutional support, and patent influence. A total of 43,503 records were retrieved from the Lens database, consolidated, and subjected to thematic screening, producing a final corpus of 27,001 publications. The main search achieved 98.45% relative coverage, while thematic screening yielded 96.1% weighted precision and 94.3% weighted recall. A multilabel taxonomy distinguished recovery technologies from physicochemical mechanisms, computational tools, enabling technologies, and environmental integration. Among technologically classified publications, CO₂-EOR and polymer flooding formed the main documentary core. Associations with reservoir simulation, mobility control, interfacial phenomena, nanotechnology, and geological carbon management revealed distinct bases of technological support and adaptation. The reconstructed geographical distribution remained concentrated, with differentiated country specializations and substantial dependence on metadata availability. Institutional analysis showed thematic overlap between universities and companies, whereas patent indicators demonstrated that scientific scale and inventive influence are not equivalent. These findings show that the evolution of EOR technologies depends on interactions among documentary scale, knowledge integration, geographical distribution, institutional support, and circulation within the patent system.

title: Beyond SAF Certification: Reconciling ISCC CORSIA and ISCC EU through Life-Cycle Carbon Accounting, Feedstock Eligibility and Double-Counting Prevention in International Aviation
abstractText: The international expansion of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) has exposed a critical distinction between sustainability certification, quantified life-cycle greenhouse gas reductions, and legal recognition of those reductions. This qualitative literature review examines the relationship between ISCC CORSIA and ISCC EU, emphasizing their different regulatory purposes, life cycle assessment methods, feedstock criteria, and controls against duplicate environmental claims. Drawing on 64 journal articles published during 2020-2026 and authoritative ICAO and European Union documents, the review synthesizes six themes: certification non-equivalence, carbon-intensity methodology, feedstock eligibility, chain-of-custody integrity, market implications, and institutional interoperability. The analysis identifies a recurrent governance error: treating possession of a recognized certificate as sufficient proof that the same emissions benefit can be claimed under multiple compliance or voluntary frameworks. It proposes a three-gate model that separates qualified physical fuel, regime-specific life-cycle calculation, and exclusive claim entitlement. Particular attention is given to the differentiated legal treatment of palm-derived materials, including palm fatty acid distillate, palm oil mill effluent, and empty palm fruit bunches. A linked physical-batch and claims-ledger architecture, supplemented by minimum evidence datasets and transparent regulatory mapping, is advanced as a practical alternative to automatic certificate equivalence. The review concludes that cross-border SAF recognition depends on auditable data exchange, explicit jurisdiction specific eligibility decisions, and prevention of double issuance, double use, and double claiming, rather than universal acceptance of any one sustainability certificate.

title: PERSISTENCE, MARGINALIZATION, AND TECHNOLOGICAL FORGETTING IN ENHANCED OIL RECOVERY: AN EVOLUTIONARY ANALYSIS OF COMPETING EOR TRAJECTORIES
abstractText: The technological evolution of Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) has traditionally been interpreted through the growth of publications and patents, although documentary expansion does not necessarily imply technological strengthening. This study investigated the processes of technological selection, documentary persistence, relative marginalization, and vulnerability to documentary technological forgetting across 26 EOR technology families between 1900 and 2026. The analysis was based on 74,454 unique records retrieved from the Lens platform and integrated structural breakpoint detection using the Pruned Exact Linear Time (PELT) algorithm, persistence, documentary renewal, documentary intensity, and relative selection metrics, as well as the composite indices Integrated Selection Index (ISI) and Technological Forgetting Index (TFI). Three robust historical breakpoints were identified (1975, 1990, and 2010), delimiting distinct phases of diversification, competitive reorganization, and technological reconfiguration. Recent growth was concentrated in Air/Flue Gas Injection, CO₂-EOR, and Water Alternating Gas (WAG), which formed the dominant technological core of the system. Air/Flue Gas Injection exhibited the highest documentary intensity (DI = 120.22 documents/year) and high documentary continuity (PIage = 0.961), whereas SAGD was the only technology to achieve consistent relative gains across all historical transitions (RSS = +3). In contrast, Alcohol Flooding, Solvent/LPG Flooding, Carbonated Water Injection, and Miscible Gas Flooding exhibited the highest levels of documentary vulnerability. The results demonstrate that persistence, renewal, and relative selection represent complementary dimensions of technological evolution and that documentary technological forgetting occurs predominantly as a gradual loss of relative relevance rather than as an abrupt disappearance of technological trajectories.

title: A validation study of an experimental ChatGPT-designed personnel selection assessment instrument in the SIRIUS-23 space mission isolation experiment
abstractText: Personnel selection for isolated and confined extreme (ICE) environments, such as space, polar, and deep-sea missions, requires reliable psychological assessments to evaluate adaptability, resilience, and teamwork under prolonged confinement. Traditional human-administered assessments, while effective, can introduce unconscious biases. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers a data-driven alternative to potentially reduce bias. This study evaluates the validity of an experimental, large language model-designed personality assessment (LLM-D) by comparing its results to a validated instrument, the Isolated and Confined Extreme Environment Questionnaire (ICE-Q). The six crew members of the SIRIUS-23 isolation experiment completed the LLM-D pre-mission and the ICE-Q during the mission. The LLM-D evaluated key psychological traits using a structured scoring system. Post-isolation, participants completed a self-reporting questionnaire (SRQ) for triangulation. Responses were scored by ChatGPT and two psychometrists. A multi-faceted statistical approach evaluated differences and agreement between ratings and instruments. Findings indicate that the experimental LLM-D, in its current form, is not valid for psychological assessment or candidate selection. Although demonstrating acceptable to high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.63–0.85; eight of 10 constructs ≥ 0.70), its estimates are constrained by sample size, and scores are significantly biased and uncorrelated with validated measures from the ICE-Q or SRQs. The LLM-D systematically measures psychological constructs other than those intended, leading to the concerning conclusion that using it would select objectively less suitable candidates for ICE missions. Contribution: These results highlight the need to redefine the instrument through qualitative analysis of AI decision-making and to realign it with ICE-Q definitions, offering critical insights into the responsible use of GenAI in high-stakes psychological assessment.

title: Reasons for discontinuing internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy-based treatment for older adults with depression: Findings from a qualitative study
abstractText: Background Online psychological interventions, particularly internet-based cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT), have proven effective in treating mental health issues such as depression and anxiety. However, participants often drop out before completing these interventions, especially in the context of ICBT for older adults. Understanding the reasons for dropout can improve engagement and the overall effectiveness of online interventions. Method Thematic analysis was employed to examine reasons for dropout from an online CBT intervention for older adults (60+). Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 9 participants who dropped out of the program. Data was analysed using thematic analysis. Results Key themes underlying dropout included technical difficulties, perceived ineffectiveness, the program’s rigid format, and symptom exacerbation. Participants also highlighted a lack of personalized support and dissatisfaction with the program’s content. Broader engagement barriers emerged as well, such as limited digital literacy, frustration with the structure, and a mismatch between participants’ expectations and the program’s offerings. Conclusion While online CBT can be an effective tool for older adults, factors like program rigidity, lack of personalization, and digital literacy challenges must be addressed to reduce dropout rates. Tailoring content and improving participant support are essential for enhancing engagement and ensuring the success of internet-based interventions for older adults.
